/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2312:- The slot-binding graph publisher (`publish_merged_bindings` in `crates/verter_session/src/meta_resolve/slot_binding_graph.rs`) publishes shallow `SemanticTypeSource` positions. Analyzer assembly leaves `AnalyzedSlotFieldBinding.payload: None` (flat locators cannot address nested `(slot, binding)` positions). Live selection among the graph-native value node: (1) closed symbolic indexed-access → `Closed(IndexedAccess)`; (2) argument-bearing named-reference use-site → `Authored(DeclBody)`; (3) named-reference head → shallow closed `Ref`; (4) otherwise the first-class `SemanticTypeSource::SyntheticSlotBinding(Arc<SyntheticCarrierKey>)` (raised as `SemanticNodeData::SyntheticBinding`, shelling to `TypeExpr::SyntheticSlotBinding`). Only the synthetic arm deepens through the content-free synthetic-binding identity.
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2313:- Consumers MUST NOT resolve a synthetic carrier's `binding_name` through `TypeRegistry` — the name is intrinsic, not a workspace alias. Reducing through the resolver would re-enter registry collection looking for a type that does not exist (the "same-name poisoning" risk).
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2314:- Explicit deepening of a synthetic carrier routes through the content-free `ShapeSubject::SyntheticBinding { id }` identity, built via `ShapeCacheKey::synthetic_binding_whole(SyntheticBindingId::from_carrier_key(&carrier), mode)`. The cache identity is the content-free `SyntheticBindingId` (`scope_canonical_id, surface_kind, slot_name, binding_name`); the carrier's `value_node` arena ordinal is value-side PROVENANCE only — re-attached at the compat boundary via `SemanticNodeData::SyntheticBinding`'s `to_carrier_key`/`raise`, never part of the cache key (two carriers differing only in `value_node` collapse onto one entry). The `ShapeSubject::TypeExpr` carrier bypass is closed structurally by the construction-sealed `NonSyntheticTypeExpr` wrapper (a `pub` newtype whose private tuple field plus fallible module-private `new` are the seal): a `TypeExpr::SyntheticSlotBinding`-carrying expression can never key a `ShapeSubject::TypeExpr` (so its `value_node` can never fold into the structural hash); a BARE top-level carrier redirects to `SyntheticBinding { id }`; a NESTED carrier (`{x: carrier}`, `carrier | null`) has no sound content-free key, so `type_expr_whole_with_context` returns `None` and the caller cache-bypasses (cold compute, no cache write — the value still flows). The carrier itself stays shallow. The ONE production consumer of the deepen route is the terminal-demand raise of the `SemanticTypeSource::SyntheticSlotBinding` source arm (`raise_synthetic_binding_source_to_hot` -> `deepen_synthetic_binding_to_hot` in `crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/semantic_source.rs`): carrier/shell modes (`Navigate`/`Shallow`/`Skeleton`) intern the terminal `SemanticNodeData::SyntheticBinding` node (shallow-by-default), while terminal-demand modes (`Expanded`/`Identity`) peek the `ShapeCacheDb` slot under the content-free key and cold-reduce from the SAME-GENERATION `value_node` seed (the seed node must exist and its minting file scope's `whole_hash` must equal that file's live hash; a stale seed fails CLOSED to the shallow carrier, no cache write; genuine-partial results are refused warm admission). The positive-proof test at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_misc0/synthetic_carrier_explicit_deepen_proof.rs` proves the content-free identity (collapse + the still-discriminating axes + the `value_node` provenance round-trip), and the in-crate rail test `crate::query_db_self_root_tests::shape_cache_db_synthetic_binding_untracked_self_root_rejects_warm_entry` proves the single-entry cache is fact-signature rail-validated.
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2315:- The retired R22 substrate — `CarrierVerdictDb`, `CarrierVerdictSlot`, `CarrierIdentity`, `CarrierVerdict`, `CarrierProvenance`, `CarrierProvenanceTable`, `CarrierValueNodeId`, the `carrier_provenance_table` field, the `carrier_verdicts` accessor on `ProjectTypeStore`, and the `crate::carrier_verdict_db` module — MUST NOT be reintroduced. The static guard at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_misc2/no_carrier_verdict_db.rs` enforces this.
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2316:- **Hover-boundary demand entry.** `VerterHost::deepen_synthetic_slot_binding(scope_canonical_id, &Arc<SyntheticCarrierKey>)` (`typeinfo/raise.rs`) is the in-process consumer entry for a slot-name hover's terminal demand: it raises the `SemanticTypeSource::SyntheticSlotBinding` source arm under `Published(Expanded)` through the one dispatch (whose terminal-demand split IS `deepen_synthetic_binding_to_hot`) and materializes through the registered typeinfo output sink — it never touches `ShapeCacheDb` or mints `ShapeCacheKey`s itself, so the route-level "ONE production consumer" contract stands. Fail-closed: an unraisable source or a deepen that fell back to the shallow carrier returns `None` and the caller keeps the typed refusal. The LSP consumes it path-precisely — ONLY the rank-matched slot's carrier bindings deepen (`features/hover_slot_deepen.rs::matched_slot_carrier_bindings`; publication stays shallow, the component-tag summary deepens nothing). Pinned by `deepen_synthetic_slot_binding_deepens_live_carrier_and_fails_closed_on_stale` (session) + `only_the_rank_matched_slots_carrier_bindings_enter_the_deepen_fan_out` (LSP).
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2318:**Architecture guards:** Structural confinement is PRIMARY (the construction-sealed `NonSyntheticTypeExpr` newtype + the sealed `MemberShapeNodeSubject(SemanticNodeId)` newtype keying the `ShapeSubject::MemberValueNode` arm + the module-private `ConstructionSeal`-fielded `ShapeSubject::SyntheticBinding` arm + the private `ShapeCacheKey.subject`/`.demand` construction in `component_meta_caches.rs` — a `ShapeSubject` (and the `ShapeCacheKey` wrapping it) is constructible ONLY through the in-module `ShapeCacheKey` constructor families, including their context/fallible forms: `type_expr_whole` / `type_expr_whole_with_context` (the latter returns `Option`, classifying bare/nested/carrier-free), `surface_member_value_whole_with_context` (the SOLE production member-shape constructor, taking a policy-admitted `&AdmittedPublishedMember` token — strictly tighter than a raw `&SurfaceMember`, so an unadmitted member cannot be routed through the sealed subject; the raw `&SurfaceMember` form is the `#[cfg(test)]`-only `surface_member_value_whole_with_context_raw`, and the test-only arbitrary-node form is `member_value_node_whole_for_test`), and `synthetic_binding_whole` / `synthetic_binding_whole_with_context`); the grep scanner is the bounded residual SYNTACTIC supplement. (1) `no_carrier_verdict_db` (file basename) at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_misc2/no_carrier_verdict_db.rs` — walks `crates/*/src/**` and asserts every retired R22 identifier is absent from production source. (1b) `synthetic_carrier_explicit_deepen_routes_through_shape_cache_key` (file basename) at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_misc2/synthetic_carrier_explicit_deepen_routes_through_shape_cache_key.rs` — a SEPARATE guard in its own file (the synthetic-deepen `value_node` scanner; relocated out of `no_carrier_verdict_db.rs`, which is the independent R22 retired-symbol guard), bans the direct `SemanticNodeId(<ident>.value_node)` ordinal-key shape (a single identifier followed by `.value_node`; the previous "legitimate cache-route" upstream-window exemption is removed — the `value_node` ordinal is value-side provenance, never a cache key). It claims ONLY that direct single-ident shape; receiver expressions, chained field access, method/index receivers, and binding indirection are OUTSIDE the matched shape and covered by the structural primary. The regular `ShapeSubject::MemberValueNode` route takes the member by reference and reads `member.value` through the sealed `MemberShapeNodeSubject` newtype, so it is structurally unmatched. Paired self-tests prove the scanner discriminates (forbidden ordinal-key shapes — including the formerly-exempt split call — match; `SemanticNodeId(0)` / `SemanticNodeId(member.id_field)` / `value_node:` field decls / serialization / the content-free `synthetic_binding_whole` route do not). (2) `synthetic_binding_cache_subject_is_content_free_and_carrier_sealed` at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/architecture_guards.rs` — asserts the `ShapeSubject::SyntheticBinding` variant carries ONLY the content-free `SyntheticBindingId` (no `value_node` / `SemanticNodeId`), the `synthetic_binding_whole` constructor builds it, and the `NonSyntheticTypeExpr` seal exists (rejecting a synthetic-carrying `TypeExpr` via the shared `type_expr_contains_synthetic_slot_binding` walker), with a discriminating self-test. (3) `synthetic_carrier_explicit_deepen_proof` (file basename) at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_misc0/synthetic_carrier_explicit_deepen_proof.rs` — positive executable proof of the content-free explicit-deepen identity: admits a deep `TypeExpr` under `ShapeCacheKey::synthetic_binding_whole(SyntheticBindingId::from_carrier_key(&carrier), mode)` and asserts two carriers differing only in `value_node` COLLAPSE onto one entry, that distinct `scope` / `slot_name` / `binding_name` / `surface_kind` / `ProjectionMode` each discriminate, and that the `value_node` provenance round-trips (`from_carrier_key` drops it, `to_carrier_key` re-attaches it); the in-crate rail test `crate::query_db_self_root_tests::shape_cache_db_synthetic_binding_untracked_self_root_rejects_warm_entry` proves the single-entry cache is fact-signature rail-validated (an untracked self-root recomputes cold, never stale-serves). (4) `no_unsanctioned_semantic_node_id_in_shape_or_materialize_key` at `crates/verter_session/tests/cases/g_cache/r6_r21_query_identity_keys.rs` — the BROADER scoped cache-key-hygiene scanner over the shape/materialize derived-`Hash` keys (`ShapeCacheKey` + `ShapeSubject` + `MaterializationCacheKey`): forbids the content/version field markers (`whole_hash`, `content_hash`, `parse_stable_hash`, `DeclIdentity`, `value_node`, …) and pins the `SemanticNodeId` allow-list to EXACTLY two positions. The TWO `SemanticNodeId`-keyed scanners — (1b) the synthetic-deepen `value_node` scanner and (4) `no_unsanctioned_semantic_node_id_in_shape_or_materialize_key` — become STRUCTURAL (compiler-enforced) and are DELETED once the key-safety newtype substrate lands (newtype the env/content hashes + seal the `SemanticNodeId`/`value_node` tuple fields); tracked at `docs/arch/key-safety-newtype-substrate-debt.md`. (1) `no_carrier_verdict_db` is a retired-symbol-absence scanner and is NOT closed by that substrate (newtyping hashes / sealing `SemanticNodeId` does not prevent reintroducing a private `CarrierVerdictDb` / `carrier_verdicts` symbol) — it REMAINS. (2) `synthetic_binding_cache_subject_is_content_free_and_carrier_sealed` and (3) `synthetic_carrier_explicit_deepen_proof` are already a structural pin and a positive executable proof, not residual scanners, so there is nothing to delete there.
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2320:## Carrier publication & the materialize boundary (PARSELOWER foundation)
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2322:The shallow-by-default publication surface stores macro type-argument bodies as session graph handles via the **macro hot mirror** (`crate::structural_carrier_producer::macro_surface`, LANDED — full contract in `/type-resolution` → "Macro Hot Mirror"), with `TypeExpr` materialised only at the output/compat boundary. The mirror is the SOLE production producer of a macro arg's structural carrier graph (keyed `(owner, whole_hash, macro_index)` → `HotTypeRef`, lazy/singleflight, PURE — no host route lookup, no dep emission); the four production macro-arg sites (`resolve_macro_payload` + probe, slot-binding extractor, `vue_exec` `defineSlots<mapped>`, `eval_env` `expand_macro_types`/`defineModel`) all read the ONE mirror and re-enter the shared dispatch from it for their terminal demand. The query-free mirror DEFERS resolution to the resolving DEMAND (codex-ruled "A/C, not B" — no side-band dep preflight on the accessor): `resolve_carrier_subject_node` resolves a `TypeOf` empty-path macro payload (`typeof config`) via `typeof_key_for`→`build_typeof`; the deferred-shell evaluator resolves a `BareRef`/`ImportType` Pick/Omit/mapped source one hop under `StructuralTransit(Navigate)`; `resolve_member_value_for_classification` resolves a bare/import carrier so `type MyStr = string` classifies `ExactConcrete`. Cross-file resolution-witness recording is at the demand: `build_typeof`'s import miss observes the owner's path-precise resolution witness and marks the result `result_is_partial`/`cache_suppress`/request-suppress-sticky (a `typeof <unresolved import>` is a `MissingDependency` → `ReturnOnly`), and the field materializer refuses `ShapeCacheDb` admission of a `TypeOf`-rooted semantic miss so a later request recovers after the dependency appears.
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-CM1-FINDINGS-BC.md:2325:- **Bounded declaration-body hot-read path (Stage 6 Option B, LANDED).** The LIVE landed hot-read surface is the thin shared `decl_body_hot_ref` accessor (`project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:1455`, over the `SemanticGraphStore` `Instantiate` memo, handle minted at the dispatch boundary over the `Instantiate` query result — `build_instantiate`'s post-processed node; the graph-bearing helper `lower_decl_body_with_provenance` produces the resolving-lowered body-SHAPE that `build_instantiate` post-processes (member-index backfill + cross-file augmentation stitch) into it; the producer never calls `HotTypeRef::new` — not a re-lowering), read by the ONE migrated graph-backed publication anchor `lower_decl_body_to_node` (`meta_resolve/projectors/macro_payload_substrate.rs`); the public `TypeExpr::Ref` (and the compat DTO surface) stays the materialised output of the two output-boundary fns `materialize_output_type_expr` / `materialize_reduced_output_type_expr` (the test-only `materialize_type_expr` `HotTypeRef` wrapper has ZERO production references — it is never a production publication boundary). Handles mint ON DEMAND at the dispatch boundary and are NEVER stored in the prepared-decl bundle — the superseded bundle-stored handle mirror (`HotPrepared*`) is DELETED. The prepared surface is fact+locator NoTypeExpr end-to-end (the lower-crate `Prepared*` DTOs carry classification facts + content-free body locators; the session `PreparedDeclBundle` stores those fact DTOs, with the memo-owned classification facts copied at prepare time). `DeclBodyMemo` records are facts+locators end to end (the two former memoized type-parameter pockets are CLOSED: `LoweredTypeDecl` is wholly `NoTypeExpr` — the stored full `type_parameters` is deleted, the `narrow_type_parameters` mirror is the sole stored type-parameter authority, and bound content re-borrows lease-only; `TypeParamBinding` is the content-free `(name, ordinal)` fact pair, likewise `NoTypeExpr`) — `LoweredTypeDecl.body` is `TypeDeclBody` (`Single(TypeBodySlot)`/`Merged` contributor SLOTS) and `LoweredValueDecl` is fully narrowed (`ValueTypeAnnotationFact` + signature/shape/enum facts + the memo-owned value `body_hash`, NoTypeExpr-witnessed); authored bodies are re-borrowed lease-only from the retained snapshot by the locator-deref worker; residual SEMANTIC reader classes per `docs/arch/authored-shape-graph-native-migration-deferral.md` (decl bodies still LOWER to typed IR transiently; only the hot READ surface is handle-native).

# C1 — Converge `ModuleResolverCore` and non-flow `TypeInfoCore`

**Status:** DRAFT — authored for maintainer review; no AMD ratifies it yet. **Class:** Foundational
(`program-dag.toml:162`). **Predecessors:** `A6`, `B1`, `B2` (`program-dag.toml:163`).

C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and the TypeScript-style resolver living in
`verter_workspace::resolver` — into the two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a
`ModuleResolverCore` that owns TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow
`TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution,
relation/inference, effective typing, recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and
exactness/completeness propagation. Neither target type exists in code today; both names describe roles
the current tree already plays under different names and in the wrong crate. C1 does not invent new
resolution semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be
identical to today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code, how many
duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform I/O
directly, and where the crate boundary sits.

C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta
publication policy (`/component-meta`). It extends nothing about `execute_relate`'s relation semantics or
`ProjectSemanticDispatch`'s five query modes — those are `Preserve`, not `Converge`, dispositions. It owns
convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, and the addition of a batched,
resumable load-outcome so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume the same kernel a blocking lifecycle
consumes today.

## Intent Contract

**Actor / problem.** Every current and future first-party consumer of Verter's type/module resolution —
the host-backed LSP session, the session-overlay (unsaved-edit) path, and the future project-aware direct
compiler (`C2`'s sealed `CompileTypeInfo`) — must resolve a symbol, import, or type to the *same* answer.
Today that guarantee is held by convention (three lifecycle adapters hand-implement the same sealed
`ResolverContext` trait with large amounts of copy-pasted delegation) and by omission (no lifecycle exists
yet that cannot block a thread on I/O), not by a structural authority that forces convergence and permits
a new I/O-free lifecycle to be added without duplicating resolution logic a fourth time.

**Required observable outcomes.**

All four proposed positions fail. Forks 1 and 3 are one coupled decision.

First, the draft is factually wrong that both modules are private: `resolver_core` is `pub mod`; only `resolver_store` is private (`crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:341-342`). That does not rescue in-place convergence.

### Fork 1 — VIOLATES

Invariant: inward, cycle-free dependency direction; compiler may depend on the semantic kernel, never on session (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/architecture.md:1110-1130`, `decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md:24-34`).

A `pub(crate)` session facade is unusable by C2. Making it public would require `verter_compiler -> verter_session`, while session already depends on compiler (`crates/verter_session/Cargo.toml:117`), creating a cycle. Compiler already depends on the ratified layer-3 kernel crate, `verter_semantic` (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:59`; `crates/verter_identity/tests/cases/workspace_dependency_layers.rs:44-47`).

“Prove extractability without extracting” is not mechanically enforceable inside this crate. The existing structural graph guard explicitly cannot see intra-crate direction (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/A5/dependency-direction.md:182-189`). A facade controls exposure, not what its implementation imports. The current context directly names scheduler state and `VerterHost` (`resolver_context.rs:183-196,700-717`).

Ruling: **EXTRACT-NOW into existing crate `verter_semantic`**, not a new `verter_typeinfo` crate. Exact boundary:

- `verter_semantic`: `ModuleResolverCore`, non-flow `TypeInfoCore`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, relation/node algorithms, dependency-neutral semantic store/value types, immutable observation contracts, and `AttemptOutcome`/`LoadSet`.
- `verter_workspace`/`verter_session`: observation capture, committed-store implementations, `VerterHost`, scheduler, I/O flights, cache-retention policy, and outer retry/commit orchestration.
- `verter_compiler`: C2’s concrete `CompileTypeInfo`, plans, facts, and anti-replay tokens.

The kernel closure must contain only layers 1–3 and exclude compiler/workspace/session/scheduler/provider. The existing Cargo-metadata closure guard is the landed structural enforcement (`workspace_dependency_layers.rs:1-18,316-350`).

### Fork 2 — VIOLATES

Invariant: environments provide immutable data observations, not resolution semantics or live I/O (`architecture.md:461,631,660-662`).

Relocating the whole `WorkspaceRead` trait is the wrong boundary. Route analysis uses only `read_file`, `file_exists`, `is_dir`, and `read_dir` (`routes.rs:195-205,250-259,660-678,868-879`). `WorkspaceRead`, however, also exposes authoritative import resolution (`traits.rs:214-280`), generations and dependency graphs (`traits.rs:347-508`), and directory/filesystem operations (`traits.rs:510-532`). Moving that interface downward would preserve live workspace authority inside the kernel and let environments continue implementing resolution semantics.

Ruling: move the six workspace-taking capture/orchestration entry points upward, but keep semantic extraction downward. Pass an owned immutable `RouteAnalysisInputs` snapshot into the existing pure extractors—already exemplified by `detect_routing_framework_from_json` and `extract_programmatic_routes` (`routes.rs:208-233,266-289`). Moving all extraction into workspace would mix semantic interpretation into a lifecycle adapter.

This does not foreclose F1: F1 can later replace the capture producer with its coherent committed snapshot without changing semantic computation. Moving `WorkspaceRead` downward would foreclose that separation; its current methods are live authority calls, not captured observations. F1 requires one coherent captured state (`architecture.md:410-422`).

### Fork 3 — VIOLATES

Invariant: compiler and semantic compute are structurally I/O-free (`contracts/input-loading.md:5-19`; `architecture.md:461`).

The marker is externally sealed, but it does not prove I/O freedom. `RequestBoundResolverContext` extends `ResolverContext` (`resolver_context.rs:780-782`), so an analogous subtrait inherits `ensure_loaded`, `ensure_indexed_ready_serve`, and the direct host escape hatch (`resolver_context.rs:261-266,700-717`). Both current request-bound implementors physically contain `&VerterHost` (`host_resolver_context.rs:81-84`; `session_resolver_context.rs:85-89`) and delegate those methods to it (`host_resolver_context.rs:264-287`). `ensure_loaded` submits to and waits on the scheduler (`host_lifecycle.rs:988-1013`).

The draft’s assertion that such a bound “does not expose” `ensure_loaded` is therefore plainly wrong (`C1-CHARTER-DRAFT.md:215-219`).

Ruling: extraction and I/O confinement are one decision. In the extracted kernel, use a separate capability-limited immutable observation interface that does **not** extend current `ResolverContext` and cannot return a host. The crate dependency firewall then makes naming `VerterHost` or the scheduler impossible. A marker may classify that interface, but the marker alone is not the proof.

### Fork 4 — VIOLATES

Invariant: whole-attempt, maximal-sound batched demand discovery and complete compile facts.

The normative contract covers compiler, resolver, and TypeInfo kernels without qualification (`contracts/input-loading.md:5-19`) and reruns the whole operation after each load wave (`contracts/input-loading.md:34-45`). ADR-011 additionally requires each attempt to report the maximal sound missing-observation set (`decisions/ADR-011-staged-compile-attempt-and-input-loading.md:19-28`).

C2 plans the complete semantic demand closure before projection (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:18`) and requires one complete result per demand (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:44-53`). A remaining type-query path must either block—violating direct project mode—or return incomplete facts, which emission must reject. Current TypeInfo projection already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` for member/JSDoc hydration (`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`), so “module/import only” is not even a clean existing boundary.

Ruling: **FULL-COVERAGE-REQUIRED** for every non-flow `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt. Internally, the two ensure functions may become central observation-or-demand choke points, but acceptance cannot be “one real load point” as the draft proposes (`C1-CHARTER-DRAFT.md:80,252-255`).

FORK 1 — **VIOLATES — EXTRACT-NOW into `verter_semantic`.**  
FORK 2 — **VIOLATES — move workspace capture upward; pass immutable route inputs downward.**  
FORK 3 — **VIOLATES — extraction plus a capability-limited observation interface; no `ResolverContext` marker.**  
FORK 4 — **VIOLATES — FULL-COVERAGE-REQUIRED for all non-flow projection-reachable operations.**

# D1 — Private sole-flow-solver foundation

**Status:** DRAFT pending maintainer ratification. **Class:** Foundational
(`governance.md` §2.3 names "flow/effective typing" explicitly as a Foundational
example area; `program-dag.toml` / `program.md:225-233`). **Predecessors:** `A3`, `B1`,
`B2` — all three `ACCEPTED` (`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:157-176,245-264,465-484`)
— and `C1`, currently `status = "READY"` but its own charter is **DRAFT, unratified**
(`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:619-638`; `charters/C1.md:3`).
D1 cannot be `BLOCK_READY` while a predecessor's charter is unratified; see Sequencing.

## Context — why this is far bigger than program.md's nine lines

`program.md:225-233` gives D1 one paragraph: build canonical graph adapters, derived
projections, a domain registry, a demand plan, binding slots, relation-authority
integration, an obligation ledger, a private finalizer, parse reacquisition, and typed
gaps — all behind a hermetic non-production boundary — so that it "preserves every
ratified supported capability" before `D2`'s cutover. Read literally that sounds like a
scaffolding exercise. **It is not**, for the same reason this program has repeatedly
found blocks larger than their summary: the paragraph describes architecture.md §9's
full target shape (§9.1-9.9), and the code it must functionally match today is real,
large, and already characterized by ~20,000 lines of pinned regression tests.

**The thing being replaced is not small.** The current effective-flow ("`FlowReturn`")
answer is produced by a private, syntax-shaped, name-keyed evaluator:

- `crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs` — 8,416 lines
- `crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs` — 733 lines
- `crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs` — 5,407 lines

— roughly 14,500 production lines — pinned by roughly 20,000 lines of characterization
tests (`flow_return_coverage_tests.rs` 3,154; `flow_return_lexical_tests.rs` 6,683;
`flow_return_tests.rs` 4,531; `flow_return_positional_tests.rs` 463;
`flow_return_root_gate_tests.rs` 680; `flow_return_frame_seal_tests.rs` 409;
`flow_gap_retraction_tests.rs` 672; `u6_flow_shape_corpus_tests.rs` 4,084). D1 must
reproduce, through a wholly different graph-native mechanism, whatever slice of that
14,500-line surface the (currently unratified — see Open Questions) A6 capability
matrix calls Supported/Stable, and must answer everything else with a typed gap at
least as precise as the eleven (`G1`-`G11`) gap classes `A3` already shipped
(`docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/A3/A3-SPEC.md` §5). That is not "scaffolding
behind a flag"; it is standing up a second, competing, complete-enough analysis engine
under the same hermetic roof.

**The target is already normatively specified, in more detail than program.md itself.**
Four documents bind D1 more precisely than the block's own paragraph:
[`contracts/flow-completeness.md`](../contracts/flow-completeness.md) (the "Flow Domain
Closure, Obligation Ledger, and Completeness Contract" — normative), `architecture.md`
§9 ("Effective typing and flow", §9.1-9.9), `decisions/ADR-001-semantic-authority-and-derived-projections.md`,
and `decisions/ADR-014-atomic-flow-cutover-and-obligation-proof.md`. This charter treats
those four as the binding shape and program.md's paragraph as their one-line summary,
consistent with how `C1.md`'s Context section treated `program.md:191-197` — effort and
breadth are not reasons to shrink a charter (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning).

**What D1 does NOT do**, stated up front because it is easy to over-read the paragraph:
it does not delete `flow_return.rs`/`flow_return_callee.rs`/`flow_slice_content.rs` (that
is `D2`'s one atomic cutover, per `ADR-014` decision 2); it does not touch any product
entry point; it does not implement nominal-identity extension (`D3`), the full
narrowing/structural-return algebra (`D4`), closure/capture join semantics (`D5`), the

    42	
    43	## 3.2 `ATOMIC_REVIEW`
    44	
    45	Use when several review-sized diffs collectively form one indivisible clean cutover.
    46	
    47	Rules:
    48	
    49	- top-level `acceptance_block_id` names the sole program block that may become accepted/landed from this window;
    50	- all layers belong to that atomic acceptance unit and have unique `layer_id` values;
    51	- private layers may repeat the acceptance block's `block_id` as internal checkpoints, or name an explicit `foundational-private-checkpoint` predecessor such as `D1`;
    52	- intermediate layers target a private integration branch, remain draft, are marked `NON_MERGEABLE_PRIVATE_LAYER`, and are unreachable from production entry points;
    53	- no intermediate layer is released, merged to trunk, or recorded as an accepted program predecessor, except an explicit program checkpoint such as D1 whose `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT` state is valid only for the final acceptance block;
    54	- exactly one final mergeable layer routes every consumer, deletes the displaced path/support machinery, and becomes the reviewed candidate;
    55	- the complete combined tip receives the block's required conformance, architecture, and adversarial/performance review;
    56	- landing preserves the exact reviewed candidate delta on the recorded landing base.
    57	
    58	`D1`/`D2` is the canonical case: D1 is a private checkpoint; D2 is the sole acceptance and landing unit.
    59	
    60	## 3.3 Parallel disjoint work
    61	
    62	Parallelism is represented by separate `LANDABLE` or `ATOMIC_REVIEW` windows, not one artificial stack. Each window declares shared owners/files/generated artifacts and integration tests. A newly discovered ownership overlap stops or serializes the affected work.

1. **Capability matrix: D1 starts against an unratified row target.** All eight `Status` cells remain `VERIFY`; such rows cannot support architecture/default claims ([capability-matrix.md:4](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/capability-matrix.md:4), [capability-matrix.md:15](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/capability-matrix.md:15), [capability-matrix.md:75](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/capability-matrix.md:75)). Therefore D1’s substantive Supported/Stable row set is empty today; its structural requirements still bind. U-1 requires ratification before the **atomic flow-cutover block**, which is D2—not before D1 starts ([implementation-lock-record.md:328](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/A6/implementation-lock-record.md:328), [implementation-lock-record.md:863](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/A6/implementation-lock-record.md:863), [program.md:231](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:231), [program.md:235](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:235)). The draft’s implication that U-1 may block D1 `BLOCK_READY` is wrong.

   Impact — ADR: no; DAG: no; program outcome: no. No program amendment; product/conformance matrix ratification remains mandatory before D2.

2. **C1 moves `flow_return.rs`, `flow_return_callee.rs`, and `dispatch_txn.rs`.** C1 orders physical relocation of `project_semantic_dispatch` as a module ([C1.md:183](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:183), [C1.md:250](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:250)). Those files are declared children of that module ([mod.rs:109](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/mod.rs:109)). C1’s named carve-outs are three `resolver_core` lifecycle-adapter pieces, not flow files ([C1.md:253](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:253)). “C1 does not own flow semantics” means relocate unchanged, not leave behind ([C1.md:352](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:352)). Conversely, `flow_slice_content.rs` is a sibling session module and does not move under C1 ([lib.rs:189](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:189)). The draft’s claimed boundary gap is not real.

   Impact — ADR: no; DAG: no; program outcome: no. No AMD; make the three filenames explicit when ratifying C1’s charter.

3. **D1 must extend the existing `ObligationRuntime`; it must not create a peer obligation authority.** The code explicitly defines one tagged runtime shared across relation, flow-return, and call domains so cycle spaces cannot diverge ([dispatch_txn.rs:1](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:1), [dispatch_txn.rs:30](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:30), [dispatch_txn.rs:211](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:211)). `ObligationRuntime` owns generic topology/pending/substitution state, while one transaction owns it plus typed domain payloads ([dispatch_txn.rs:874](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:874), [dispatch_txn.rs:1890](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:1890)). D1 may add the contract’s plan-origin/domain/dependency/discharge-evidence representation, but subordinate to that one runtime—not as a separately constructed ledger ([flow-completeness.md:40](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/flow-completeness.md:40), [architecture.md:765](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/architecture.md:765)). Consequently, the draft’s demand for zero diff in `dispatch_txn.rs` is wrong; legacy behavior stays unchanged, but the shared mechanism must evolve.

   Impact — ADR: no; DAG: no; program outcome: no. No amendment.

4. **The effective-flow rows cannot presently be enumerated from A6.** The matrix has no flow-capability discriminator or explicit `FlowReturn` operation—only eight broad product rows ([capability-matrix.md:13](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/capability-matrix.md:13)). Inferring only `TypeInfo / TypeAtPosition` would be unsound: that row visibly references flow ([capability-matrix.md:19](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/capability-matrix.md:19)), but Vue macro projection also directly demands body-derived `FlowReturn` ([tsc_projection.rs:734](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/vue_macro_codegen/tsc_projection.rs:734)), and the public whole-function flow-return operation has no matrix row at all ([host_flow_return_audit.rs:2](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/host_flow_return_audit.rs:2), [host_flow_return_audit.rs:82](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/host_flow_return_audit.rs:82)). Therefore the enforceable Supported/Stable effective-flow set is empty, while the underlying flow-bearing operation set is undefined. Add explicit flow rows or an explicit row-to-flow-subcapability mapping before ratification.

   Impact — ADR: no; DAG: no; program outcome: no—the existing outcome is being made enforceable. Formal product/conformance matrix revision and ratification: yes; program AMD: no.

5. **Stable binding slots are the existing identity mechanism, not a new abstraction.** Within one body, `SkeletonBindingId` is the lexical binding slot ([flow/mod.rs:75](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/mod.rs:75)); the canonical graph maps it deterministically to a binding node ([flow_graph.rs:71](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs:71), [flow_graph.rs:182](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs:182)). Cross-frame identity already exists as `(defining_function, binding_slot)` in `FlowBindingIdentity` ([function_program.rs:265](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/function_program.rs:265)). `FlowNodeId` is merely a dense graph-local node index, not the binding identity itself ([flow_graph.rs:54](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_semantic/src/analysis/flow/flow_graph.rs:54)). Thus D1 keys state by graph/body identity plus `SkeletonBindingId`, using `FlowBindingIdentity` across frames; D3 completes coverage and domain use. Minting a parallel slot type is forbidden.

   Impact — ADR: no; DAG: no; program outcome: no. No amendment.

6. **AMD-001 never gated D1 implementation start; it gated the first stack window and D1 entering `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT`, and that prerequisite is now discharged.** That is AMD-001’s exact timing ([AMD-001:43](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/amendments/AMD-001-stack-window-validator-prerequisite.md:43), [maintainer-rulings.md:170](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/maintainer-rulings.md:170)). Commit `f46de1b6a` delivered all four artifacts: composite validation ([stack-window-lib.mjs:281](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:281)), the D1/D2 structural transition tests ([validate-stack-window.test.mjs:257](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/validate-stack-window.test.mjs:257)), script registration ([package.json:26](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/package.json:26)), and CI path wiring ([ci.yml:60](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/.github/workflows/ci.yml:60)). D2 still requires an actual validated `ATOMIC_REVIEW` snapshot with D1 private and D2 as sole acceptance block ([stacked-prs.md:49](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:49)). Fresh test execution was sandbox-blocked at temporary-directory creation, so this is landed-source verification, not a new green-run claim.

   Impact — ADR: no; DAG: no; program outcome: no. AMD-001 already records the governing change; no further amendment is required.

opposite-shaped BLOCKING bridge (`produce_vue_macro_codegen`), not "adding tokens to an existing staged
path" as program.md's summary implies. C2's predecessors B3, B5 and C1 are themselves unimplemented.

## The five forks

**A. Fate of `VueMacroSemanticInput` and `verter_macro_dto`'s `MacroRuntimeBundle`/`MacroTscBundle`.**
Deleted outright, or retained as an internal emit-stage shape? Guessing wrong either breaks C3's
already-locked vocabulary or leaves a compatibility shim alive — and this codebase deletes superseded
paths rather than keeping both.

**B. Is B6 a real, missing predecessor of C2?** `contracts/compile-transaction.md:8-9`'s stage 1 appears
to need `PreparedCarrier`, which B6 owns, yet the DAG does not list B6 as a C2 predecessor. Either the
DAG has a missing edge or the contract does not really need it. **This one changes a DAG edge if you rule
it real — say so explicitly.**

**C. Which crate owns the concrete project-aware `CompileTypeInfo` lifecycle variant?** This depends on
C1's extraction, which has now been RULED: C1 extracts the module-resolver / non-flow TypeInfo kernel into
the EXISTING `verter_semantic` crate, with a capability-limited observation interface and a closed
inherent gateway (`TypeInfoCore::attempt`). Read
/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md and

**D. How many first-party lifecycle modes does `CompileTypeInfo` have — three or five?** ADR-003 and the
charter disagree. Resolve from the ratified source.

**E. Do the new anti-replay tokens need the private-`sealed`/single-construction-point pattern?** Note
what the C1 addendum established: Rust has no friend-crate exception, so a private-supertrait seal and a
foreign implementor are mutually exclusive — a sealing design that requires an out-of-crate implementor is
impossible. Rule on the token pattern with that constraint in view.

- Concise, file:line throughout. End with five verdict lines.

The draft is right that C2 is greenfield, but three details are wrong or stale: `verter_macro_dto/src/lib.rs` ends at line 579, not 1355; `CompileTarget` is a `pub(crate)` bitflags type, not a sealed single-construction token (`crates/verter_compiler/src/compile/types.rs:5-52`); and C1’s rulings now settle `CompileTypeInfo` ownership.

### A. Delete the legacy bridge types

Delete `VueMacroSemanticInput`, `MacroRuntimeBundle`, and `MacroTscBundle` as named aggregate contracts. Do not retain them as an emit-stage compatibility shape.

The old enum aggregates optional Runtime/TSC bundles without plan, profile, basis, or demand identity (`crates/verter_compiler/src/compile/types.rs:105-141`). Its bundle outcomes also retain pre-transaction failure states (`crates/verter_macro_dto/src/lib.rs:19-52,346-369`), whereas C3 requires one token-bound `DemandResult` per demand and rejects every top-level non-success before publication (`docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C3.md:38-72`). Emission consumes validated complete facts, not another semantic envelope (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:12-15,44-53`).

Keep `verter_macro_dto` as the neutral owner permitted by `architecture.md:1123-1127`, and reuse/refactor useful row primitives into C3’s exact `MacroRuntimeProjection`/`MacroTypeProductProjection` vocabulary. The three legacy aggregate types themselves go.

**Governance:** accepted ADR unchanged; DAG unchanged; program outcome unchanged.

### B. B6 is a real missing predecessor

C2’s first normative stage returns the exact `PreparedCarrier` (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:8-15`), and B6 expressly owns preparation/reuse lifecycle and makes the direct core ready for semantic projection (`charters/B6.md:5-12`). A separate C2-local preparation type would violate the one-path cutover.

Add the edge `B6 -> C2`. The normalized direct predecessor set should be `["B3", "B6", "C1"]`; B5 is already transitively required by B6 (`charters/B6.md:3`). The current DAG is therefore wrong at `program-dag.toml:165-169`.

**Governance:** accepted ADR unchanged; **DAG edge changed—formal amendment required**; program outcome unchanged.

### C. `verter_compiler` owns `CompileTypeInfo`

The public concrete facade and its private project-aware lifecycle variant live in `verter_compiler`. `verter_semantic` owns `TypeInfoCore`, `ObservationSnapshot`, and the closed `TypeInfoCore::attempt` gateway.

That allocation was already explicit in the C1 ruling (`ARCH-RULING-C1-FOUR-FORKS.md:14431-14437`). The addendum requires composition: `CompileTypeInfo` consumes a semantic-owned `ObservationSnapshot`; it does not implement the sealed observation trait (`ARCH-ADDENDUM-C1-THREE-GAPS.md:34-45`). This also follows the existing dependency direction: compiler depends on semantic (`crates/verter_compiler/Cargo.toml:51-60`), while session depends on compiler (`crates/verter_session/Cargo.toml:114-129`).

**Governance:** accepted ADR unchanged; DAG unchanged; program outcome unchanged.

### D. Five construction modes, three orchestration classes

The closed first-party vocabulary is five: local, captured-project, in-memory, engine-snapshot, and validated-precomputed (`architecture.md:623-635`; ADR-003:11-17).

The three entries in `compile-transaction.md:68-74` classify observation/I/O orchestration:

- local direct → local;
- direct project → captured-project or in-memory;
- managed → engine-snapshot.

Validated-precomputed is a separately validated first-party ingress, not another loading/retry policy. It remains optional and cannot become a general public persistence constructor without the required consumer ADR (`architecture.md:1011-1030,1221`).

Thus the draft is wrong that the accepted documents prescribe competing enum counts.

**Governance:** accepted ADR unchanged; DAG unchanged; program outcome unchanged.

### E. Private nominal tokens plus type-state; no sealed trait

Yes, tokens require a structural single-mint boundary—but not a private-supertrait seal.

Place concrete token types behind a private compiler module, with private fields and no public constructors. `plan()` alone mints plan/subplan tokens; `project()` or the validated-precomputed admission path alone constructs complete facts. `emit()` accepts the resulting typed plan/complete-facts states and performs the two required identity validations (`contracts/compile-transaction.md:22-53`). Digest equality prevents replay between legitimately minted plans; private construction and type-state prevent external fabrication and stage skipping.

No foreign token implementor is required, so the C1 friend-crate impossibility does not arise. The draft’s `CompileTarget` analogy is factually wrong: it is merely crate-private bitflags, and its own comment refers to internal construction points in the plural (`crates/verter_compiler/src/compile/types.rs:17-28`).

**Governance:** accepted ADR unchanged; DAG unchanged; program outcome unchanged.

A — **DELETE `VueMacroSemanticInput`, `MacroRuntimeBundle`, and `MacroTscBundle`; retain only refactored C3 payload primitives.**  
B — **ADD `B6 -> C2`; formal DAG amendment required.**  
C — **OWN `CompileTypeInfo` in `verter_compiler`; compose semantic-owned snapshots and call `TypeInfoCore::attempt`.**  
D — **FIVE first-party construction modes, grouped into THREE orchestration classes.**  
E — **USE private nominal tokens and type-state with one mint path; do not use a cross-crate sealed trait.**

> This banner is removed when the program completes and the target architecture is described here directly.

Verter = a Vue compiler + Language Server Protocol (LSP) implementation. Converts Vue Single File Components (SFCs) to valid TSX (TypeScript type-checks them) and compiles templates to optimized render functions. Unlike Volar, Verter generates real valid TSX, not virtual files.

Hybrid Rust + TypeScript monorepo: Rust crates own carrier parsing, runtime and IDE code generation, the shared semantic session, and the LSP server (`verter_lsp` binary, stdio); TypeScript packages provide editor integration, TypeScript-provider adapters, protocol bindings, and bundler orchestration.

## Architecture

Detailed module reference, key files, and implementation specifics live in domain skills: `/type-resolution`, `/type-cache-architecture`, `/component-meta`, `/compiler-codegen`, `/host-session`, `/architecture`.

### Shared Optimized Codebase (CRITICAL)

Verter is one shared optimized codebase, not separate semantic implementations per consumer.

- Improvements land in the lowest reusable owner crate that can correctly serve all consumers.
- `verter_session` + shared workspace/VFS integration are the authority for host-backed loading, invalidation, dependency tracking, cache reuse.
- `verter_semantic` + `verter_compiler` own reusable semantics, lowering, codegen.
- `verter_session::resolver_core` owns the host-backed resolver stack + type-resolution orchestration.
- `verter_audit` is the leaf observability substrate (depends only on `verter_span`, no back-edge; lower crates emit through `current_observer()` (TLS) without knowing whether a `HostAuditRuntime` is installed); the concrete host runtime lives in `verter_session` — full ownership inventory in `/audit-infrastructure`.
- `verter_protocol` owns transport-facing schema DTOs; `verter_ffi` remains the thin native/WASM adapter layer.
- Consumer packages (`@verter/component-meta`, LSP, MCP, unplugin, playground) consume the shared substrate, not their own semantic forks.

Architectural consequence:

- A perf/correctness fix found in one surface is implemented in the shared owner layer whenever the behavior is reusable.
- Consumer-local wrappers stay thin and do not bypass shared parsing, analysis, resolution, or cache ownership.

**Exactly one type-resolution engine.** `SemanticQueryKey` → `ProjectSemanticDispatch::execute` → `SemanticGraphStore`, five query modes (`Identity`/`Navigate`/`Shallow`/`Expanded`/`Skeleton`) — the SOLE query-time type resolver. OXC is the syntax/lowering front-end ONLY (declaration bodies lower to `TypeExpr` lazily on first semantic demand through the scheduler-retained parse snapshot — the `DeclBodyMemo` owned by `IndexedReady`); OXC must never resolve types at query time. Any second query-time resolution path — a parallel `resolve_type` engine, a per-surface walker, a re-parse-and-resolve, an OXC element/frontier resolver — is a rule violation: delete it, route through the shared resolver. Two engines diverge; divergence is the bug/hang class.

**Audit infrastructure:** Rust-first deterministic per-request observability for every audited `VerterHost` entry-point (component-meta, type-resolution, compile, analyze, workspace ops, LSP handlers, MCP tools, bundler batches). TS bindings in `packages/types/audit.generated.ts`; opt-in via `HostConfig::audit_enabled + footprint_capture`. See `/audit-infrastructure` and [`docs/audit-footprint/`](docs/audit-footprint/).

Guards: `verter_audit_no_upward_deps`, `audit_substrate_isolation`, `audit_observer_single_accessor`. The former single-engine `no_new_*` shrinking-ledger scanners retired with the deleted parser-owned `type_surface` engine; the single-engine invariant is now held structurally (the compiler consumes only the dependency-neutral macro DTO) plus the Vue macro boundary suite registered under "Vue Macro Semantic Boundary" in `CRITICAL_RULE_GUARDS`.

### Build Philosophy (CRITICAL)

Same end-state philosophy as `binary-exploring-lamport.md`. Core rules:

The authoritative boundary is capability-based, not directory-based: dependency-neutral semantic compute moves to `verter_semantic`; live host observation, cache admission, retention, publication, audit, and I/O remain in `verter_session` ([ADR-015:16-32](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/decisions/ADR-015-binding-dependency-direction.md:16), [C1 revised:341-348](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/C1-CHARTER-REVISED.md:341>)).

- `flow_slice_content.rs` — MOVES whole. Its complete surface—`FlowSliceSelection`, every `Slice*`/`Gated*`/`FrameShadowedName` type, `SignatureScope`, `Lowerer`, `build_function_type_param_clause`, `build_flow_slice_content`, and all lowering helpers—is owned, arena-free semantic IR/lowering over OXC and semantic/type-expression inputs; it contains no host, store, scheduler, cache, audit, or I/O authority ([flow_slice_content.rs:53-79](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs:53), [flow_slice_content.rs:81-159](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs:81), [flow_slice_content.rs:1471-1489](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/flow_slice_content.rs:1471)). Its being a sibling module is irrelevant to architectural ownership.

- `flow_return_callee.rs` — MOVES whole. `ReturnOrigin`, `ClauseParamInference`, `CalleeClauseParam`, `CalleeClause`, `CalleeClauseLookup`, `CallValue`, `SignatureCall`, `HeldCallee`, and `unmodeled_position_marker` are pure semantic transfer/evaluation machinery. The file depends only on the relocating semantic dispatcher/query vocabulary and function-program facts ([flow_return_callee.rs:84-91](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs:84), [flow_return_callee.rs:112-248](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs:112), [flow_return_callee.rs:436-733](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return_callee.rs:436)).

- `dispatch_txn.rs` — SPLITS; it does not move whole. The semantic transaction symbols move: `SessionId`, `InferenceOccurrence`, `StrictFamilyConfig`, `RelationStep`, `RelationAssumptionEvidence`, `ObligationIdentity`, the frame/pending/SCC topology, `ObligationReentryStack`, `ObligationPendingLedger`, `Provisional*`, `ObligationRuntime`, inference-session machinery, `SessionAdmissionLedger`, return-equation state, and their algorithms ([dispatch_txn.rs:78-265](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:78), [dispatch_txn.rs:396-561](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:396), [dispatch_txn.rs:795-959](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:795)). Session retains `InlineRelationFlight`/`InlineFlowReturnFlight`/`InlineResolveCallFlight`, `ObservedGraphSelfRoot`, `CompletedSccMember`, `CompletedFlowReturnMember`, `CompletedResolveCallMember`, and completed-member publication queues ([dispatch_txn.rs:269-314](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:269), [dispatch_txn.rs:1763-1904](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:1763)). Consequently `RelationFrameState`, `FlowReturnFrameState`, `ResolveCallFrameState`, the three `*PendingState` types, the three `*DomainRuntime` types, and `CheckerDispatchTransaction` split internally: semantic state moves; flight/root/publication fields stay in a session wrapper.

- `flow_return.rs` — SPLITS. Move the result/value and evaluator authority: `FunctionReturnNode`, `ConsumerFold`, `FlowRootClose`, `FlowEvaluationOutcome`, `FlowFramePop`, `MemberDemandFilter`, `FlowBinderEnv`, `GuardNarrowing`, `NodeDisjointness`, `FlowEvaluator`, `FlowContribution`, `FlowBreakExit`, `ScopeShadow`, `FlowLayerState`, `Positional`, all pure helper functions, SCC/fixed-point computation, narrowing/join logic, and the `FlowEvaluator` algorithms ([flow_return.rs:42-297](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:42), [flow_return.rs:1594-1809](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:1594), [flow_return.rs:2559-3200](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:2559)). Session retains the live-capture/admission portions of `flow_return_context_for`, `resolve_call_context_for`, `execute_semantic_expression_source`, `execute_function_return_source`, `served_callee_clause`, `execute_flow_return`, `execute_flow_return_root`, `execute_flow_return_cold_build`, `flow_return_drain_completed_members`, and `build_flow_return` ([flow_return.rs:302-428](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:302), [flow_return.rs:592-713](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:592), [flow_return.rs:900-1137](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:900)). The mixed `evaluate_flow_return` symbol must decompose: immutable demand/evaluation logic moves, while indexed serving, fact capture, flow-slice store lookup, audit, and content reacquisition at lines 1971-2113 stay above ([flow_return.rs:1921-2113](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:1921)). Likewise, inline-flight claims/abort/publication inside `flow_frame_open`/`flow_frame_pop` stay in session while the frame/SCC transition math moves. `FlowEvaluator::direct_callee_clause` and `eval_call_via_resolve_call` move only after their live `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` calls are replaced by captured immutable observations ([flow_return.rs:7238-7254](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:7238), [flow_return.rs:7781-7790](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/flow_return.rs:7781)).

There is no cross-block ownership problem around `ObligationRuntime`. C1 relocates/separates the existing authority; D1, whose predecessor is C1, then extends that same semantic-owned symbol—never a peer ledger ([program.md:225-231](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:225), [dispatch_txn.rs:879-959](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/crates/verter_session/src/project_semantic_dispatch/dispatch_txn.rs:879)). D1 remains inseparable from D2 under ADR-014 ([ADR-014:13-19](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/decisions/ADR-014-atomic-flow-cutover-and-obligation-proof.md:13)).

This changes no accepted ADR, DAG edge, or program outcome. Structural enforcement remains the crate dependency firewall and sealed/capability-limited boundaries, never a new name-keyed scanner ([C1 revised:362-364](</private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/C1-CHARTER-REVISED.md:362>)).

```text
flow_return.rs         | SPLITS | semantic values/evaluator/SCC math → verter_semantic; capture/cache/admission/audit → verter_session
flow_return_callee.rs  | MOVES  | entire file → verter_semantic
dispatch_txn.rs        | SPLITS | ObligationRuntime + semantic transaction state → verter_semantic; flight/root/publication carriers → verter_session
flow_slice_content.rs  | MOVES  | entire file → verter_semantic
```

   582	  // -- Review verdict identity binding (nothing previously bound a verdict to
   583	  // the exact candidate it was issued against — see templates/program-state.
   584	  // template.toml's conformance_reviewed_sha/architecture_reviewed_sha/
   585	  // adversarial_reviewed_sha comment). Structural, so it runs in BOTH modes:
   586	  // a PASS mandate must carry a well-formed reviewed SHA equal to the row's
   587	  // CURRENT candidate_sha (a fix round, a rebase, or a restack that advances
   588	  // candidate_sha without a fresh review leaves the old PASS stale); a
   589	  // non-PASS mandate must carry no reviewed SHA at all. Existence of the
   590	  // reviewed SHA as a real git commit object is checked separately, in live
   591	  // mode only, by verifyLiveGitIdentities below.

   596	      const reviewedSha = b[shaField];
   597	      if (mandate === "PASS") {
   598	        if (!(typeof reviewedSha === "string" && SHA_RE.test(reviewedSha))) {

   600	            `state block ${id} has ${mandateField} = PASS but ${shaField} is not a non-empty 40-char lowercase git object id: ${JSON.stringify(reviewedSha ?? "")} — a PASS verdict must bind the exact candidate it was issued against`,
   601	          );
   602	          continue;
   603	        }

   606	            `state block ${id} has ${mandateField} = PASS with ${shaField} = ${reviewedSha} but candidate_sha is not a non-empty 40-char lowercase git object id — cannot verify the verdict is bound to the current candidate`,

   609	        }

   612	            `state block ${id} has ${mandateField} = PASS but ${shaField} = ${reviewedSha} does not equal candidate_sha = ${b.candidate_sha} — the verdict was issued against a different candidate and is stale`,
   613	          );

   617	          `state block ${id} has ${mandateField} = ${JSON.stringify(mandate)} (not PASS) but ${shaField} = ${JSON.stringify(reviewedSha)} is non-empty — a non-PASS mandate must not carry a reviewed candidate SHA`,
   618	        );

   773	  // governance.md:181 mandates this validator pass "before a block ... enters

   776	  // digest. So the gated transitions carry status-dependent obligations:

   778	  //   PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT         — exact base/candidate identity and the
   779	  //                                charter/context/evidence digests exist and
   780	  //                                are well-formed;
   781	  //   PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT         — additionally: the status is permitted ONLY
   782	  //                                for a DAG block whose class is exactly
   783	  //                                "foundational-private-checkpoint" (program-
   784	  //                                dag.toml declares exactly one — D1), and
   785	  //                                every review mandate is PASS (program.md §7:

   795	  //                                INVALIDATED, missing, or empty mandate
   796	  //                                rejects. NOT_REQUIRED is permitted ONLY for

   817	      "ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED",

   842	      requireDigest("evidence_digest");

   846	      // entry charter (charters/A0.md) and the contracts/baseline-lock.md §2

   849	      // the digest is REQUIRED at every gated transition of that block

   853	      // artifact. A zero-root or multi-root DAG is already reported by the

   857	      if (
   858	        dagRoots.length === 1 &&

"")} is not a non-empty 64-char lowercase SHA-256 — ${id} is the DAG's entry (root) block and its entry-lock record (contracts/baseline-lock.md §2; the entry charter's first required-evidence item) must be digest-bound before review, acceptance recommendation, or acceptance`,
   865	          );

   872	        // "an explicit program checkpoint such as D1"). Any other block in

   874	        // (including a block absent from the DAG) fails closed.

   877	          v(

   879	          );
   880	        }
   881	      }
   882	      if (
   883	        b.status === "ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED" ||
   884	        b.status === "ACCEPTED" ||
   885	        b.status === "PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT"

   902	            v(
   903	              `state block ${id} is ${b.status} but ${field} is NOT_REQUIRED and DAG class ${JSON.stringify(blockClass)} does not permit it — NOT_REQUIRED is permitted only for architecture_review on a subsystem-class block (governance.md §2.2); a foundational* block requires all three review mandates PASS on one exact candidate SHA/tree (governance.md:106,277)`,

   935	  // -- Amendment authority gate
   936	  // templates/program-state.template.toml — `enabling_amendment` names the AMD-ID
   937	  // whose ratification is this block's execution authority ("" when none is
   938	  // needed). Until that amendment's own docs/arch/refactor/rev11/amendments/
   939	  // <AMD-ID>-*.md Status line is ratified, the amendment "has no execution
   940	  // authority" (its own wording) and the block it introduced must go no further
   941	  // than LOCKED. This was previously recorded only as free-text prose in a
   942	  // block's `notes` field — BV1 was unlocked and dispatched on DAG predecessor
   943	  // satisfaction alone while its enabling AMD-005 sat PROPOSED, because nothing
   944	  // read the prose. This check makes the dependency machine-enforced.
   945	  {
   946	    const AMENDMENT_GATED_STATUSES = new Set([
   947	      "READY",
   948	      "IN_PROGRESS",
   949	      "REVIEW",
   950	      "ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED",
   951	      "ACCEPTED",
   952	    ]);
   953	    const amendmentsDir = join(dirname(opts.dag), "amendments");
   954	    const statusCache = new Map(); // amdId -> {path, ratified, statusText} | {error}
   955	
   956	    const resolveAmendmentStatus = (amdId) => {
   957	      if (statusCache.has(amdId)) return statusCache.get(amdId);
   958	      const record = (result) => {
   959	        statusCache.set(amdId, result);
   960	        return result;
   961	      };
   962	      let entries;
   963	      try {
   964	        entries = readdirSync(amendmentsDir);
   965	      } catch (err) {
   966	        return record({
   967	          error: `amendments directory ${amendmentsDir} could not be read: ${err.message}`,
   968	        });
   969	      }
   970	      const matches = entries
   971	        .filter((name) => name.startsWith(`${amdId}-`) && name.endsWith(".md"))
   972	        .sort();
   973	      if (matches.length !== 1) {
   974	        return record({
   975	          error: `expected exactly one file matching ${amdId}-*.md under ${amendmentsDir}, found ${matches.length}${matches.length ? ` [${matches.join(", ")}]` : ""}`,
   976	        });
   977	      }
   978	      const filePath = join(amendmentsDir, matches[0]);
   979	      let text;
   980	      try {
   981	        text = readFileSync(filePath, "utf8");
   982	      } catch (err) {
   983	        return record({ error: `amendment file ${filePath} could not be read: ${err.message}` });
   984	      }
   985	      const lines = text.split(/\r?\n/);
   986	      const start = lines.findIndex((l) => l.startsWith("**Status:**"));
   987	      if (start === -1) {
   988	        return record({
   989	          error: `amendment file ${filePath} has no **Status:** line — its ratification state cannot be parsed`,
   990	        });
   991	      }
   992	      // The Status field is a markdown paragraph: the declaring line through the
   993	      // next blank line (AMD-009's "**RATIFIED ...**" and AMD-001's multi-line
   994	      // "NOT part of ..." wrap onto following lines).
   995	      const paragraph = [];
   996	      for (let i = start; i < lines.length; i++) {
   997	        paragraph.push(lines[i]);
   998	        if (lines[i].trim() === "") break;
   999	      }
  1000	      const statusText = paragraph.join(" ").trim();
  1001	      // "NOT RATIFIED" (AMD-005) wins over any other "ratified" mention in the
  1002	      // same paragraph; bare "ratified"/"maintainer-ratified" (AMD-002/003/004,
  1003	      // AMD-006/007/008/009/010) is ratified; anything else — including
  1004	      // AMD-001's "Registered amendment ... NOT part of the verbatim-
  1005	      // reconstructed authority set", which never uses the ratified verb at
  1006	      // all — defaults to not-ratified. This is a classification, not a parse
  1007	      // failure: only a missing Status line above is unparseable.
  1008	      let ratified;
  1009	      if (/\bnot\s+ratified\b/i.test(statusText)) ratified = false;
  1010	      else if (/\bratified\b/i.test(statusText)) ratified = true;
  1011	      else ratified = false;
  1012	      // Report only the paragraph's first line in violation text — readable, and
  1013	      // every existing amendment's ratification verdict is already decided by
  1014	      // its first line; classification above still sees the full paragraph.
  1015	      return record({ path: filePath, ratified, statusText: lines[start].trim() });
  1016	    };

  1018	    for (const [id, b] of stateById) {
  1019	      const amdId = typeof b.enabling_amendment === "string" ? b.enabling_amendment.trim() : "";
  1020	      if (amdId === "") continue;
  1021	      const resolved = resolveAmendmentStatus(amdId);

  1024	          `state block ${id} declares enabling_amendment ${JSON.stringify(amdId)} but ${resolved.error}`,
  1025	        );
  1026	        continue;
  1027	      }

  1030	      if (typeof b.status === "string" && AMENDMENT_GATED_STATUSES.has(b.status)) {

  1035	      }

  1039	        );
  1040	      }
  1041	    }
  1042	  }

  1044	  // -- Single IN_PROGRESS block, bound to current_block

  1119	            );

  1132	    // Evidence-digest content binding. Shape-checking a digest proves only
  1133	    // that a binding was recorded, not that it binds the right bytes — a
  1134	    // well-formed but WRONG evidence_digest previously printed OK. When the
  1135	    // ledger claims evidence root(s), every declared root must be a real
  1136	    // directory and every resolved evidence_digest must match an artifact

  1138	    // different block series can live under different roots).

  1140	    // `evidence_roots` (an array) is the plural form; `evidence_root` (a
  1141	    // single string) keeps working unchanged for a lone root. Declaring both
  1142	    // with evidence_root non-empty is ambiguous and rejected rather than

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:186:1. [most severe — adversarial] The conformance harness's invoke-vue-oracle.mjs never passes vapor/ssr to compileScript, so ALL harness-generated Vapor goldens were compiled as non-Vapor by the official compiler (proven: {vapor:true} vs {} produce different __vapor markers on the real pinned rc.3 compiler). BV0's candidate then changed Verter's OWN production code (script/process.rs, 3 sites) to match those wrong goldens — removing the __vapor:true marker from real non-SSR Vapor builds. This is load-bearing at runtime (isVaporComponent gates VDOM<->Vapor interop). A new unit test locks the wrong behavior in. The seed matrix cannot detect it because candidate and golden are wrong identically (two bugs cancelling out).
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:291:- Completion fence: top-level live-host results record touched dependency facts, revalidate before publish, retry at most 3 times on mid-flight changes; never warm shared caches with torn provisional results; cancelled, superseded, interrupted, budget-exceeded, or partial results are never promoted warm.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:789:   276	notes = "Gap-analysis-only block: every one of BF1's 7 numbered exit criteria and all owned-scope bullets independently verified already satisfied by the previously-landed, maintainer-ratified AMD-005 package. REOPEN #1 (legitimate, new finding not previously reviewed): the parallelism consult found exit criterion #6 (BF2 performance cells frozen before BF2 work begins) was unmet — performance-gates.toml had no BF2 cells. Resolved by measuring the already-authored, BF1-owned official-case enumeration tool (generate-official-case-manifests.mjs) against the pinned oracle sources — a legitimate before-BF2-exists reference measurement, not criterion-selection-after-candidate-measurement — freezing BF2_VUE_ORACLE_MANIFEST_GENERATE/BF2_SVELTE_ORACLE_MANIFEST_GENERATE (10-invocation session, wall/RSS bounds, SHA-256 output-oracle, exact-equality work counters, operationally-proven zero-network via a live curl-denial control). First review pass: architecture BLOCKING (cells mislabeled as covering golden/compiler-invocation generation, which was never measured); fixed by rescoping the operation text to enumeration/classification only and adding an explicit open/deferred row in performance-impact.md for the heavier compiler-invocation+golden workload (matching the existing BV1/BS1/B6/C4 deferred-row pattern). Reattested PASS, no threshold values changed, no scope creep. candidate_sha == accepted_sha exactly (no landing squash needed beyond the one already-squashed commit). Prior review record: architecture PASS (DAG sequencing B1->BF1->BF2->BF3->{B2,B3} confirmed coherent, zero production diff, emitter-mapping dispositions spot-checked), adversarial found one BLOCKING governance finding (AMD-005 §15.1's ratification quotation cited the wrong reviewed-package SHA — pre-fix ce1d0e4688 instead of PASS-reattested 7442bb9060; citation-only, substance always correct) — escalated per STOP conditions, architecture-authorized as non-discretionary record repair (no new maintainer ratification required, governance §10), landed as standalone commit f1b59d2dd. AMD-005 (Framework Compiler Conformance Rescope) itself maintainer-ratified and landed at 34fe8167f (housekeeping squash of the original four-commit landing sequence — content byte-identical, tree unchanged; superseded pre-fix candidate ce1d0e4688/1ff1f83d8e, reviewed package 7442bb9060/69502487b, ratified bundle aa757eecc/0c078357b, original ratification-record commit ade8a301b, preserved on branch backup/pre-amd005-squash). BF2 next legal once this transition is validated."

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:9413:**Demand-driven workspace-symbol completeness**: ordinary hover/completion/definition keep only editor-active/import-observed carriers in the provider. References and rename are different: neither tsserver nor tsgo can prove a workspace-wide result unless every framework source in the initiating carrier's configured project is represented. On the first such request, Verter reads immutable configured-project membership. Tsserver proves the frontier by promoting every current store advertisement through one `activate_carrier_members` transaction plus one interactive plugin refresh. TSGO never treats that editor-tsserver store as its witness, and proves TWO independent things about its own provider graph. (1) **Roots**: every expected carrier has receipt-gated, owner-matching IDE direct-open state. The API companion is deliberately not demanded here — the interactive IDE path never opens it for the file under the cursor, so demanding it would gate the frontier on a companion neither arm activates. (2) **Import closure**: for every carrier-import edge reachable from those carriers — direct imports, dynamic module references, and the `export … from` graph through rewritten barrels — the target's API companion (or the barrel's rewritten shadow buffer) is both LIVE and CURRENT. Roots alone prove each carrier's own symbols are in the Program, not that a cross-carrier reference RESOLVES: an importer's buffer imports the rewritten `{carrier}.verter.ts` specifier, so an unopened — or stale — API companion silently drops that importer from a project-wide answer. Liveness is the committed loaded flag; currency is a ROLE-SPECIFIC witness (the identity of the API declarations actually delivered to this provider, which only an API delivery may write — the state-wide commit stamp advances with IDE-only receipts and cannot stand in for it). An interactive IDE sync carries the liveness flag forward (that buffer really is still open) and re-observes the current projection, so an API-NEUTRAL edit stays ready with no reopen while a public-surface edit fails closed until publication delivers the new declarations. **Every writer of a shadow buffer must record the delivery it performed** — the source identity it built from AND the owner the live resolver reports — because the barrel re-publication leg skips an already-live shadow and is therefore not a recovery path: a state that sets only the liveness flag makes a delivered barrel read as undelivered-and-unowned, and the closure then refuses every project-wide references/rename answer for the rest of the session. This includes the OPEN-document own-path sync (`sync_self_file_shadow_state`), which serves the same rewritten projection when a user simply opens the barrel `.ts` in the editor; it recomputes the binding from the live resolver rather than clearing it, so `Unresolved` means ownership is genuinely unpublished. Carriers that are not import targets — a standalone initiating carrier, the file under the cursor — are never gated, and neither are targets outside the configured project. If the frontier is incomplete, the request signals scanner priority and fails closed instead of joining compilation or returning partial references/edits. The activated frontier stays warm for later workspace-symbol requests.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:9853:- Cache-validation staleness is enforced by the `ReadSetSignature.facts` path-precise fact signature on cache entries. Warm hits revalidate every recorded fact against the live `StoreView` before returning; stale entries miss and force a cold rebuild.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:9871:**Captured resolution root (C5a).** The snapshot also stamps the workspace's immutable published resolution world (`Option<Arc<verter_workspace::CapturedResolutionWorld>>`, captured O(1) in the same `PreBuildTokenInputs` read window via `WorkspaceRead::capture_resolution_world`: the current base root plus, for a session population, that session's overlay root). It is the SOLE authority for the `ResolveImportsFactRef::Resolution` arm — `HostStoreView::validates_resolution_fact` (shared by `validates_resolve_imports_domain` and its overlay-aware `_for_content_hash` sibling; `RequestStoreView` routes resolution facts straight to the base view because the completion overlay carries no resolver observations). A view with NO captured world validates no resolution fact. It stays OUT of the token because validity is fact-precise (world IDENTITY is barred from being a cross-root warm-validity oracle) and because a cold compute publishes replacement worlds through its OWN work (a first observation of any path records an evidence baseline), which would self-fence exactly like the additive generations. Residual, owned by C4/C5b: a view captured between a content mutation and the reader-driven evidence refresh holds a root that has not yet observed the change, so it keeps validating the pre-mutation witness until the refresh advances the fact.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round2-scope-consult-ruling.md:9873:**Handle-backed dimensions stay out of the token for DIFFERENT reasons:** `ResolvedImportFactsDb` is content-addressed — its key carries `content_hash`, so a new version is a new key and a fixed handle reads correctly (immutable-by-key). `RouteDb` is NOT content-addressed (its keys carry no content hash, and evict/clear/replace reuse the same key) — it stays out because every value it hands out is validated per candidate against the reading view through the candidate's own recorded `fact_dep_signature`, so an evict/replace yields a conservative fail-closed MISS, never a stale positive. The per-candidate signature comparison IS the validity rail, so the token needs no `RouteDb` generation. The route-surface FACT domain does not read `RouteDb` at all: its sole arm (`StoreView::validates_route_surface_domain`) compares the recorded `expected_hash` against the augmentation-index fingerprint snapshot captured on the view's artifact root.
