docs/arch/refactor/rev11/evidence/vue-known-defect-correction/reviews/round1-reopen-scoping-ruling.md:17:1. [most severe — adversarial] The conformance harness's invoke-vue-oracle.mjs never passes vapor/ssr to compileScript, so ALL harness-generated Vapor goldens were compiled as non-Vapor by the official compiler (proven: {vapor:true} vs {} produce different __vapor markers on the real pinned rc.3 compiler). BV0's candidate then changed Verter's OWN production code (script/process.rs, 3 sites) to match those wrong goldens — removing the __vapor:true marker from real non-SSR Vapor builds. This is load-bearing at runtime (isVaporComponent gates VDOM<->Vapor interop). A new unit test locks the wrong behavior in. The seed matrix cannot detect it because candidate and golden are wrong identically (two bugs cancelling out).

crates/verter_workspace/tool-output-allowlist.toml:120:rationale = "BF2 seed-matrix conformance harness (#[cfg(test, feature = \"bf2-authoritative\")]) — reads the committed golden manifest/records and Vue fixture TEST FIXTURES off disk, and reads/writes the committed per-cell code-digest baseline JSON (a TEST FIXTURE, not semantic/VFS state) for the assembled-map composition regression pin. crates/verter_workspace/tool-output-allowlist.toml:124:rationale = "Svelte official-conformance golden inventory (#[cfg(test, feature = \"bf2-authoritative\")]) — reads the committed golden manifest, each DIGEST-ADDRESSED record under goldens/records/, and the Svelte fixture source each record names, all TEST FIXTURES off disk. The record set is data-driven from the manifest at runtime, so the reads cannot be `include_str!` (a digest lookup is not a compile-time path); each read is followed by a SHA-256 verification, which is the point of reading the real bytes. Sibling of the `bf2_seed_matrix.rs` entry below, whose Vue half does the same for the same reason. Never workspace/semantic state, never the VFS."
crates/verter_workspace/tool-output-allowlist.toml:128:rationale = "PublicApi/TSC/declaration observation under the real TypeScript compiler (#[cfg(test, feature = \"bf2-authoritative\")]) — reads the committed golden manifest and the digest-addressed Vue records it names, TEST FIXTURES off disk, to assert every record pins the same official framework version the observation runs against. Data-driven from the manifest at runtime, so not expressible as `include_str!`. Never workspace/semantic state, never the VFS."

     3	// A golden record binds, beyond the oracle domain and fixture:
     4	//  - the generator's GIT identity (repo commit + tree at generation time,
     5	//    plus whether any generation-relevant path was dirty) — traceability of
     6	//    which committed code produced the set;

     8	//    entry script plus every local module it transitively imports — so

    10	//    invokers, oracle-install gate, golden store, …) changes the recorded
    11	//    identity and a stale committed set fails --check until regenerated
    12	//    (the previous script-only digest missed every non-entry module);
    13	//  - the exact REALIZED-closure digest of the isolated oracle installation
    14	//    the compilers loaded from (oracle-install.mjs) — the physical
    15	//    enumeration digest, not the lock's claim.
    16	//
    17	// Comparison semantics at --check: implementation and closure digests are
    18	// content-bound (identical for identical trees) and compare STRICTLY —
    19	// they are the binding force. The git commit/tree/dirty fields are
    20	// generation-TIME identity: an honest regeneration at a later commit of an
    21	// unchanged implementation must not read as drift, so --check normalizes

    87	export function generationImplementationFiles(entryPath) {
    88	  const seen = new Set();

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:8:This contract makes Revision 11 executable by an orchestrator agent without turning the agent into architecture, repository, or review authority.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:10:The authority package states what must become true. The repository and accepted evidence state what is currently true. The orchestrator may never fill a gap between them by assumption.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:16:- **Maintainer:** human or explicitly designated repository authority that can accept architecture, gates, blocks, and merges.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:17:- **Orchestrator:** one coordinating agent/context that owns sequencing, program-state mutation, worker assignment, evidence collection, and stop/rescope reporting.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:21:The orchestrator may also implement a block when assigned, but it cannot provide that block's only substantive review, cannot self-accept any block or gate, and cannot accept its own work.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:34:A mismatch does not become invisible merely because work appears correct. Without an explicit maintainer exception, a substituted runtime may inspect and report but cannot represent an Opus-specific Foundational result as accepted. Multiple instances of one model are not automatically independent evidence.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:40:1. read `README.md`, `ORCHESTRATOR.md`, `program-dag.toml`, `governance.md`, this contract, and the current block charter;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:44:5. inspect the actual local repository, remotes, branch, full SHA/tree, dirty/untracked/submodule state, worktrees, open local branches, and available GitHub/CI permissions;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:45:6. initialize or validate `program-state.toml` with `tools/validate_program_state.py`;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:46:7. confirm that only the next legal block is marked `READY`;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:47:8. stop if package validation, repository identity, predecessor state, or authority ownership is ambiguous.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:49:A web page, prompt summary, prior conversation, branch label, or short SHA is not authoritative repository state.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:53:A fresh Revision 11 handoff authorizes **only `A0`**.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:55:The orchestrator does not start `A1`, implementation tracks, or a broad repository rewrite in the same unreviewed act. It completes the `A0` evidence packet, updates program state, returns the result, and follows the maintainer's accepted sequencing process.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:88:- no subagent spawned merely to restate, summarize, or generically double-check the orchestrator's work;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:89:- role-mandated independent reviews use clean contexts and direct evidence, not the implementor's conclusion.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:98:- never force-pushes an accepted, queued, or shared branch without invalidating affected state and reviews;

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:128:The orchestrator never reports `PASS` or `LAND_READY` merely because it believes the design is good. It reports the actual validated state and missing proof.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:132:Stop and return `BLOCKED` or `RESCOPE_REQUIRED` when any of these occurs:

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:162:Raw command output, profiles, benchmark samples, generated manifests, review reports, range-diffs, landing-equivalence proofs, and lock records are stored at stable paths and addressed by digest. Summaries point to raw evidence and do not replace it.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:4:**Architecture authority:** `program-dag.toml`, never PR topology.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:8:Use a single PR when one bounded reviewable candidate is enough. Use a short stack when dependency ordering or an atomic cutover is materially easier to review in layers.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:10:A stack is transport. It cannot add, remove, or reorder program predecessors, split a program acceptance unit silently, or make an incomplete cutover releasable.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:16:The mutable window records `program_state_basis_digest`, the digest of the last validated program state **before** that stack is attached. `previous_stack_snapshot_digest` links a restacked successor to the prior immutable snapshot, or is `NOT_APPLICABLE` for the first window. These one-way references avoid hash cycles.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:18:Every layer has a unique `layer_id`; `block_id` names the program block whose charter/acceptance unit owns it. Every review and CI event binds to an immutable **StackSnapshotId**, defined as the SHA-256 of the fully resolved validated stack-window file. The file contains every exact base/head/tree, patch, generated-output, and evidence digest. Any changed input creates a new snapshot and invalidates affected approval.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:20:After a snapshot is attached, current `program-state.toml` stores the stack ID, StackSnapshotId, and the program block's final/current layer index. Same-block private sublayers remain detailed in the stack window rather than becoming duplicate program-ledger blocks; an explicit program block such as `D1` retains its own `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT` state. The pre-stack basis file is never rewritten. For `ACTIVE`, `FROZEN_FOR_REVIEW`, and `LAND_READY` windows, `tools/validate_stack_window.py --current-program-state ...` cross-validates the mutable ledger against the immutable snapshot. A PR label or web UI is not sufficient state.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:22:A stack-window snapshot is not the landing receipt. Actual landing is recorded by the block's validated landing-equivalence proof and the subsequent program-state transition. A used or invalidated stack snapshot is retained as evidence and replaced by a new window when work remains.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:28:Use only when every layer is independently safe and releasable. The layers form one connected dependency path; true DAG siblings use separate windows. `acceptance_block_id` is empty and each `block_id` appears once.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:140:`candidate_sha/tree` remains the exact cumulative candidate reviewers inspected. `accepted_sha/tree` records the actual landed commit and full repository tree and may differ after a reviewed rebase, squash, merge commit, or merge-queue base advance. docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:3:**Status:** Normative dependency-ordered implementation authority.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:11:The program is a DAG of bounded clean cutovers. A block may start when every predecessor has its required accepted state and the validated `program-state.toml` marks it `READY`/`BLOCK_READY`. A dependent upper layer may instead perform contingent `READY`/`IN_PROGRESS`/`REVIEW` work only when each unaccepted predecessor is a lower layer in the same validated immutable stack snapshot. It cannot become `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED` or `ACCEPTED` until those predecessors are formally satisfied and the upper candidate is restacked/revalidated on the accepted base. Except for the explicit `D1` private checkpoint, accepted block state means the predecessor is integrated on the intended lineage. `D1` is reviewed on the bounded `D2` integration branch and is never merged/released independently; `D2` is the atomic landing unit. Parallel work is legal only when cutover closures, writable worktrees, and shared generated/owner surfaces are disjoint or explicitly serialized.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:13:A pull-request stack is transport only. Bounded stack windows may linearize one short dependency path for review, but they do not create semantic predecessor authority. A program-wide mega-stack is prohibited. Atomic private layers land only through their final atomic candidate.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:67:**Exit:** one exact entry SHA/tree and lineage; no floating or equivalence claim; only legal next Gate 0 work is exposed in program state. `A6`, not `A0`, accepts the implementation baseline after Gate 0 source changes.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:89:A2C is not executable. Its reachable DAG row is retained as terminal historical state with status `SUPERSEDED`. The rejected completion candidates and incomplete implementation remain unlanded historical evidence and transfer no correctness, performance, mutation, or test result.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:91:**Exit:** none. Exact structural completion and G10 discrimination are debt `FR-D8`, owned by D6 / `U6.LOOP_CLOSURE`; heavy work resumes only after D6 has a closed, code-first carrier inventory. The demanded `FunctionFlowGraph` remains the sole completion reducer, and no syntax-only classifier or second completion authority may be introduced.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:107:Instrumentation is leaf-only, bounded, and disabled-overhead measured. It does not become semantic authority.

Migrate every current compiler consumer in the bounded family and delete source-sized `eval_source`/blank-buffer ownership in the same accepted cutover.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:173:## B5 — Borrowed one-shot compiler atomic cutover
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:177:Introduce the borrowed direct boundary over the surviving shared frontend, planner, units, mappings, and framework algorithms. Keep arenas/local state owner-affine, construct no managed/session/provider/audit infrastructure, materialize only requested terminal artifacts, separate pure Rust and FFI paths, migrate every current direct/standalone caller, and delete the displaced public/direct route in the same accepted cutover.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:185:Add explicit borrowed/owned preparation, prepare-once/emit-many, inspectable retained weight, safe drop, direct batch ownership, deterministic aggregation, and no implicit project/provider/global state. Prove all three direct regimes use the same accepted parser/planner/unit/mapping/codegen core and delete any transition-only adapters.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:205:**Exit:** project-aware compilation cannot accept another semantic engine or stale/mismatched facts.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:223:# 7. Track D — Atomic sole effective-flow solver
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:229:On the bounded `D2` integration branch, behind a hermetic non-production test boundary only, implement canonical graph adapters, deterministic derived projections, static domain registry, demand plan, stable binding slots, integration with the shared relation/inference authority, obligation ledger, private complete finalizer, exact parse reacquisition, and typed gaps. The private replacement contains no name-keyed or flow-private relation authority.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:231:No product entry point or selectable runtime flag may reach this foundation. `D1` may receive checkpoint review approval but must not merge or release independently from `D2`. Before `D2`, it must satisfy every effective-flow capability row declared Supported/Stable in the `A6` matrix, or that row must receive an explicit reviewed breaking maturity/compatibility decision. Experimental/unsupported rows may remain typed gaps according to their contract.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:233:**Exit:** the minimum replacement preserves every ratified supported capability, safely answers its covered cases, and fails unsupported cases without a second production authority.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:239:In one accepted candidate:
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:241:- route every effective-flow product operation to the new solver;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:242:- delete the syntax-shaped evaluator, name-keyed state, duplicate control/completion/relation/effect paths, caches, tasks, metrics, flags, guards, and migration comments;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:244:- preserve every `A6`-ratified Supported/Stable effective-flow capability and its public failure contract;
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:247:**Exit:** one graph authority and one production solver. This block is indivisible.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:249:## D3 — Shared relation authority and binding/product domains
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:253:Extend the already-shared relation authority with nominal identities including unique symbols and tri-state comparability; complete stable binding slots, one transfer/join per domain, deterministic worklist, and connected budgets. No flow-private relation/name authority may exist after `D2`.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:271:Close debt `FR-D8` by deriving exact structural completion and G10 discrimination on the sole demanded `FunctionFlowGraph`, then add deterministic selected-frontier loop convergence, loop-summary edges, state routing, and final clean semantics on that same graph. Heavy completion work may begin only after the D6 lock contains a closed, code-first carrier inventory. Do not reconstruct completion meaning from syntax or create another graph/classifier.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:315:## F1 — One committed input and coherent snapshot authority
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:319:Reconcile current VFS/registered-source/workspace publication into one authority; use short immutable-root commits; keep parse/compile/provider work outside the write critical section; preserve ordered document mutation.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:345:Keep hits/tiny dependent work inline; fork/chunk only coarse owned work; schedule compact commands to owner-affine parse/semantic state; bound queues/fan-out/stacks; reserve interactive capacity; support local/WASM execution without semantic divergence.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:377:Publish generated companion and required `SourceProjectionMap` atomically; wait only for requested facts; validate observed document/project/config/provider/mapping/dependency stamps; bound channels and protect interactive capacity.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:385:Preserve `StyleSyntaxIr` where it owns syntax; inventory specialized fast paths, preprocessors, CodeTransform mappings, and all consumers. A specialized path survives only when it shares authority and wins equivalent-work proof.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:437:Run every locked absolute SLO, self no-regression, work/copy/allocation, boundary, and competitor/Pareto cell. The primary direct suite must meet its locked best-in-class target. A miss is blocking; it cannot be waived by a post-result ADR. If the product/equivalent-work premise was materially wrong, amend the architecture and Implementation Lock Record under the blind recalibration rule, invalidate the affected candidate evidence, and restart the cell/block.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:444:Allocator, arena pooling, LTO/PGO, SIMD, hashing/container, or executor specialization may proceed only without reopening authority/lifetime boundaries. If opened, it must be accepted before `L4`.
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:450:Make code, architecture, ADRs, capability truth, protocols, and tests agree; remove obsolete plans/charters/shims/guards/campaign comments; pass final exact-SHA conformance, architecture, adversarial performance/memory, and maintainer acceptance.

docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program.md:470:The remedy is an amended contract/ADR/charter and renewed review—not a hidden flag, shim, broad trait, duplicate cache, parallel implementation, or outcome-driven threshold.

   180

   321	- one surviving production implementation;
   322	- every in-scope caller migrated;
   323	- old declaration/implementation/cache/task/metric/flag/dependency/re-export/wire field/fixture removed or explicitly retained under a real compatibility obligation;
   324	- compiler/build errors used as caller inventory;
   325	- no runtime switch, shadow evaluator, parser fork, alternate resolver, or duplicate cache-correctness authority;
   326	- no migration-only scanner/allowlist/guard;
   327	- historical comments cleaned;
   328	- API/auto-trait/compatibility changes documented;
   329	- behavior, work, performance, memory, and failure evidence executed;
   330	- negative net conceptual complexity unless explicitly ratified.
   331	
   332	Intermediate branch commits may be broken. Private replacement machinery may exist on the implementation branch and be exercised by hermetic tests. It must remain unreachable from production entry points until the atomic cutover, and it is deleted or becomes the sole path in the accepted merge. The accepted merge is not releasable until the cutover is complete.
   333	
   334	`D1` is the sole exception to the ordinary predecessor-integration rule: it is a reviewed private checkpoint on the bounded `D2` branch and cannot land independently. The `D2` sole-flow-solver cutover is indivisible: routing all public consumers and deleting the old evaluator occur in one accepted candidate. Later semantic coverage is added only inside the surviving solver.
   335	
   336	# 13. Evidence independence
     8	This contract makes Revision 11 executable by an orchestrator agent without turning the agent into architecture, repository, or review authority.
     9	
    10	The authority package states what must become true. The repository and accepted evidence state what is currently true. The orchestrator may never fill a gap between them by assumption.
    11	
    12	# 2. Required principals
    13	
    14	Every run names:
    15	
    16	- **Maintainer:** human or explicitly designated repository authority that can accept architecture, gates, blocks, and merges.
    17	- **Orchestrator:** one coordinating agent/context that owns sequencing, program-state mutation, worker assignment, evidence collection, and stop/rescope reporting.
    18	- **Workers:** scoped implementor, scoper, or investigator contexts.
    19	- **Review mandates:** conformance, architecture, and adversarial/performance contexts as required by `governance.md`.
    20	
    21	The orchestrator may also implement a block when assigned, but it cannot provide that block's only substantive review, cannot self-accept any block or gate, and cannot accept its own work.
    22	
    23	# 3. Model adapter identity
    24	
    25	The durable contract is model-independent. The supplied Opus adapter requests the fixed ID `claude-opus-5` and records:
    26	
    27	- requested model ID;
    28	- actual model ID;
    29	- orchestrator runtime and exact runtime version;
    30	- provider;
    31	- fallback or substitution;
    32	- any explicit maintainer exception.
    33	
    34	A mismatch does not become invisible merely because work appears correct. Without an explicit maintainer exception, a substituted runtime may inspect and report but cannot represent an Opus-specific Foundational result as accepted. Multiple instances of one model are not automatically independent evidence.
    35	
    36	# 4. Trust bootstrap
    37	
    38	Before repository mutation, the orchestrator must:
    39	
    40	1. read `README.md`, `ORCHESTRATOR.md`, `program-dag.toml`, `governance.md`, this contract, and the current block charter;
    41	2. run `python3 tools/validate_package.py` against the extracted package;
    42	3. compute and record the package manifest digest;
    43	4. record the requested and actual model, orchestrator runtime/version, and provider identity, including any fallback or substitution;
    44	5. inspect the actual local repository, remotes, branch, full SHA/tree, dirty/untracked/submodule state, worktrees, open local branches, and available GitHub/CI permissions;
    45	6. initialize or validate `program-state.toml` with `tools/validate_program_state.py`;
    46	7. confirm that only the next legal block is marked `READY`;
    47	8. stop if package validation, repository identity, predecessor state, or authority ownership is ambiguous.
    48	
    49	A web page, prompt summary, prior conversation, branch label, or short SHA is not authoritative repository state.
    50	
    51	# 5. First-run rule
    52	
    53	A fresh Revision 11 handoff authorizes **only `A0`**.
    54	
    55	The orchestrator does not start `A1`, implementation tracks, or a broad repository rewrite in the same unreviewed act. It completes the `A0` evidence packet, updates program state, returns the result, and follows the maintainer's accepted sequencing process.
    56	
    57	After `A0`, the orchestrator may continue through later blocks only when:
    58	
    59	- every direct predecessor is accepted in program state, or the block is contingent `READY`/`IN_PROGRESS`/`REVIEW` work over an exact lower layer in the same validated stack snapshot;
    60	- the block is explicitly `READY`;
    61	- the exact charter and context packet are accepted;
    62	- required permissions, branch/worktree, tests, and review mandates exist;
    63	- no unresolved architecture deviation or competing owner change blocks it.
    64	
    65	# 6. Context packet
    66	
    67	Every non-trivial worker receives an immutable packet based on `templates/context-packet.md` containing:
    68	
    69	- authority package and A6 lock digests;
    70	- exact baseline/base/candidate identities;
    71	- block, predecessors, charter digest, and stack position;
    72	- current authority/readers/writers and source references;
    73	- allowed write set and forbidden ownership changes;
    74	- required commands, evidence, deletion set, output format, and stop conditions;
    75	- one assigned role and review-independence constraints.
    76	
   128	The orchestrator never reports `PASS` or `LAND_READY` merely because it believes the design is good. It reports the actual validated state and missing proof.
   129	
   130	# 10. Mandatory stop conditions
   131	
   132	Stop and return `BLOCKED` or `RESCOPE_REQUIRED` when any of these occurs:
   133	
   134	- package, manifest, DAG, program-state, charter, or performance-gate validation fails;
   135	- actual checkout differs from the locked source and affected evidence has not been refreshed;
   136	- dirty/unowned work or a competing PR/branch touches the same authority;
   137	- a required command executes zero intended work or cannot be proven non-vacuous;
   138	- current source disproves an architecture assumption;
   139	- the true consumer/cutover closure is wider than the charter;
   140	- a public/protocol/compatibility obligation is newly discovered;
   141	- a benchmark premise or oracle is invalid;
   142	- a worker requires forbidden permissions, ambient I/O, secret access, or destructive history changes;
   143	- an atomic block would leave two production paths or an independently mergeable private layer;
   144	- required independent review cannot be obtained.
   145	
   146	The remedy is a source-backed deviation/rescope record, not a shim, hidden flag, weakened assertion, or unilateral architecture edit.
   147	
   148	# 11. Maintainer-only decisions
   149	
   150	The orchestrator may recommend but cannot self-authorize:
   151	
   152	- package adoption/supersession;
   153	- accepted ADR or architecture amendment;
   154	- `A6` acceptance;
   155	- gate weakening or benchmark premise recalibration;
   156	- formal block rescope or DAG amendment;
   157	- irreversible public compatibility/protocol policy;
   158	- merge/land/release when repository policy requires maintainer approval.
   159	
   160	# 12. Evidence custody
   161	
   162	Raw command output, profiles, benchmark samples, generated manifests, review reports, range-diffs, landing-equivalence proofs, and lock records are stored at stable paths and addressed by digest. Summaries point to raw evidence and do not replace it.
   163	
   164	A result created from a different SHA, tree, toolchain, profile, corpus, or stack base is not silently relabeled as current evidence.
     1	# Stacked Pull Request, Restack, and Atomic Landing Contract
     2	
     3	**Status:** Normative delivery contract.  
     4	**Architecture authority:** `program-dag.toml`, never PR topology.
     5	
     6	# 1. Decision
     7	
     8	Use a single PR when one bounded reviewable candidate is enough. Use a short stack when dependency ordering or an atomic cutover is materially easier to review in layers.
     9	
    10	A stack is transport. It cannot add, remove, or reorder program predecessors, split a program acceptance unit silently, or make an incomplete cutover releasable.
    11	
    12	# 2. Stack window and immutable snapshot
    13	
    14	Before creating branches, copy `templates/stack-window.template.toml`, resolve it, and validate it with `tools/validate_stack_window.py`.
    15	
    16	The mutable window records `program_state_basis_digest`, the digest of the last validated program state **before** that stack is attached. `previous_stack_snapshot_digest` links a restacked successor to the prior immutable snapshot, or is `NOT_APPLICABLE` for the first window. These one-way references avoid hash cycles.
    17	
    18	Every layer has a unique `layer_id`; `block_id` names the program block whose charter/acceptance unit owns it. Every review and CI event binds to an immutable **StackSnapshotId**, defined as the SHA-256 of the fully resolved validated stack-window file. The file contains every exact base/head/tree, patch, generated-output, and evidence digest. Any changed input creates a new snapshot and invalidates affected approval.
    19	
    20	After a snapshot is attached, current `program-state.toml` stores the stack ID, StackSnapshotId, and the program block's final/current layer index. Same-block private sublayers remain detailed in the stack window rather than becoming duplicate program-ledger blocks; an explicit program block such as `D1` retains its own `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT` state. The pre-stack basis file is never rewritten. For `ACTIVE`, `FROZEN_FOR_REVIEW`, and `LAND_READY` windows, `tools/validate_stack_window.py --current-program-state ...` cross-validates the mutable ledger against the immutable snapshot. A PR label or web UI is not sufficient state.
    21	
    22	A stack-window snapshot is not the landing receipt. Actual landing is recorded by the block's validated landing-equivalence proof and the subsequent program-state transition. A used or invalidated stack snapshot is retained as evidence and replaced by a new window when work remains.
    23	
    24	# 3. Modes
    25	
    26	## 3.1 `LANDABLE`
    27	
    28	Use only when every layer is independently safe and releasable. The layers form one connected dependency path; true DAG siblings use separate windows. `acceptance_block_id` is empty and each `block_id` appears once.
    29	
    30	Each layer:
    31	
    32	- maps to one accepted block charter;
    33	- has every external semantic predecessor accepted and may depend on an unaccepted predecessor only when that predecessor is a lower layer in the same validated snapshot;
    34	- preserves one production implementation and every current Supported/Stable contract;
    35	- passes its own charter checks on the cumulative tree;
    36	- contains its own required deletions and compatibility handling;
    37	- may land bottom-up without leaving a transitional public state.
    38	
    39	An upper layer may be `READY`, `IN_PROGRESS`, or `REVIEW` while a lower in-window predecessor is unaccepted. It may not become `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED` or `ACCEPTED` until every semantic predecessor is formally `ACCEPTED`/`PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT`, the lower landing has occurred, the upper layer has been restacked on the new base, and affected checks/reviews have revalidated the new exact candidate.
    40	
    41	An upper layer is never accepted merely because the top of the stack is green.
    42	
    43	## 3.2 `ATOMIC_REVIEW`
    44	
    45	Use when several review-sized diffs collectively form one indivisible clean cutover.
    46	
    47	Rules:
    48	
    49	- top-level `acceptance_block_id` names the sole program block that may become accepted/landed from this window;
    50	- all layers belong to that atomic acceptance unit and have unique `layer_id` values;
    51	- private layers may repeat the acceptance block's `block_id` as internal checkpoints, or name an explicit `foundational-private-checkpoint` predecessor such as `D1`;
    52	- intermediate layers target a private integration branch, remain draft, are marked `NON_MERGEABLE_PRIVATE_LAYER`, and are unreachable from production entry points;
    53	- no intermediate layer is released, merged to trunk, or recorded as an accepted program predecessor, except an explicit program checkpoint such as D1 whose `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT` state is valid only for the final acceptance block;
    54	- exactly one final mergeable layer routes every consumer, deletes the displaced path/support machinery, and becomes the reviewed candidate;
    55	- the complete combined tip receives the block's required conformance, architecture, and adversarial/performance review;
    56	- landing preserves the exact reviewed candidate delta on the recorded landing base.
    57	
    58	`D1`/`D2` is the canonical case: D1 is a private checkpoint; D2 is the sole acceptance and landing unit.
    59	
    60	## 3.3 Parallel disjoint work
    61	
    62	Parallelism is represented by separate `LANDABLE` or `ATOMIC_REVIEW` windows, not one artificial stack. Each window declares shared owners/files/generated artifacts and integration tests. A newly discovered ownership overlap stops or serializes the affected work.
    85	- Branch/PR metadata includes stack ID, mode, layer index, block ID, exact base/head/tree, charter digest, and snapshot digest.
    86	- Accepted evidence never depends on uncommitted or untracked changes.
    87	
    88	# 6. CI and proof
    89	
    90	Every mergeable layer runs:
    91	
    92	1. layer-specific tests/static checks;
    93	2. every charter check applicable to the cumulative tree from stack root through that layer;
    94	3. non-vacuous execution and generated-file cleanliness proof;
    95	4. relevant performance/memory/work gates;
    96	5. dependency, architecture, compatibility, and failure checks required by its block.
    97	
    98	The top `LANDABLE` layer additionally runs the declared stack-integration suite. The final `ATOMIC_REVIEW` layer runs full atomic-cutover proof, including one-production-path and deletion assertions.
    99	
   100	`LAND_READY` means all mergeable layers are green on the named immutable snapshot and the one currently eligible landing block is `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED`: the bottom layer for `LANDABLE`, or the final acceptance block for `ATOMIC_REVIEW`. Green upper `LANDABLE` layers remain `REVIEW`, not accepted in advance.
   101	
   102	Evidence from an older base, snapshot, toolchain, profile, or corpus is not silently reused.
   103	
   104	# 7. Lower-layer change and cascading restack
   105	
   106	When a lower layer changes:
   107	
   108	1. fix the layer where the defect belongs; never hide it in an upper workaround;
   109	2. restack bottom-to-top;
   110	3. record old/new base SHA/tree, canonical patch digest, range-diff, candidate tree, generated diff, evidence digest, and every manual conflict resolution;
   111	4. set `previous_stack_snapshot_digest` to the replaced snapshot and mint a new StackSnapshotId;
   112	5. mark all affected upper candidates/reviews `INVALIDATED`/revalidation-required;
   113	6. rerun required CI on every new cumulative tree;
   114	7. obtain impact-bounded reattestation from every required review mandate on the new exact candidate/snapshot.
   115	
   116	No approval transfers automatically. Tree/patch equivalence can make reattestation small, but the new exact identity must be named.

    11	
    12	## Context — why this is bigger than program.md's five lines

    15	use immutable observation views, return batched `NeedInputs`, exclude flow. Read literally that sounds
    16	like an in-place refactor. **It is not.** The four rulings resolve every genuine fork in the direction
    17	that costs the most, and the charter says so plainly rather than understating it:
    18	
    19	1. **This is a real crate extraction, now, not a deferred one.** `resolver_core` (`pub mod`, 59 files —
    20	   including `component_meta/` (6 files) and `component_meta_query_engine/` (14 files): verified, neither
    21	   holds a `&VerterHost`/`Arc<VerterHost>` field or parameter in production code, only doc-comment mentions
    22	   and `#[cfg(test)]` `VerterHost::new` fixture construction identical to the pattern already accepted for

    24	   wildcard, not a carve-out — see the convergence map below),
    25	   the private `resolver_store` module, and the `pub(crate)` `project_semantic_dispatch` module —
    26	   all three currently living inside `verter_session` (`crates/verter_session/src/lib.rs:332,341-344`)
    27	   — physically relocate into the existing `verter_semantic` crate (layer 3). So does
    28	   `verter_workspace::resolver::ProjectResolver` (`crates/verter_workspace/src/resolver.rs`, 2122
    29	   lines), the TypeScript-style module resolver wrongly homed in the scheduler/tsgo-dependent
    30	   `verter_workspace` crate today. This is a multi-crate structural move touching `verter_session`'s
    31	   module tree, `verter_workspace`'s module tree, `verter_semantic`'s Cargo.toml dependency edges, and
    32	   the landed dependency-layers closure guard — not a `pub(crate)` facade behind which nothing moves.
    33	2. **The `NeedInputs`/`AttemptOutcome` cutover is full-coverage, not a first cut.** Every non-flow
    34	   `ModuleResolverCore`/`TypeInfoCore` operation reachable from a C2 projection attempt must support the
    35	   batched outcome — not just the two `ensure_loaded`/`ensure_indexed_ready_serve` call sites the prior
    36	   draft scoped it to. TypeInfo projection already reaches `ensure_indexed_ready_serve` today
    37	   (`crates/verter_session/src/typeinfo/shallow_surface.rs:179-193`), so "module/import resolution only"
    38	   was never even a clean existing boundary to cut at.
    39	
    40	Effort and breadth are not reasons to shrink this (`CLAUDE.md` → Planning: "Time constraints,
    41	implementation size, migration breadth... are not valid reasons to weaken the design"). The charter
    42	states the true scope instead of preserving the five-line framing that would mislead whoever picks this
    43	up. C1 converges the current host-backed module/type-resolution stack — `verter_session::resolver_core`,
    44	`verter_session::resolver_store`, `ProjectSemanticDispatch`, and `verter_workspace::resolver` — into the
    45	two target logical owners named in `architecture.md` §8.1: a `ModuleResolverCore` that owns
    46	TypeScript-style module/path/package resolution, and a non-flow `TypeInfoCore` that owns authored-node
    47	traversal, binder/name/reference semantics, substitution, relation/inference, effective typing,
    48	recursion/work budgets, query-specific projection, and exactness/completeness propagation. Neither
    49	target type exists in code today; both names describe roles the current tree already plays under
    50	different names, in the wrong crate, with the wrong I/O coupling. C1 does not invent new resolution
    51	semantics — every module/name/type/relation answer the converged kernel gives must be identical to
    52	today's answer for every existing lifecycle. It changes who owns the code (crate, not just module), how
    53	many duplicate implementations of the same lifecycle-adapter shape exist, whether the kernel can perform
    54	I/O directly, and where the crate boundary sits.
    55	
    56	C1 does not own flow semantics (`D1`–`D8`), Vue/Svelte macro projection (`C3`), the staged
    57	prepare/plan/project/emit compile transaction or its anti-replay tokens (`C2`), or component-meta

    61	`AttemptOutcome`. It owns convergence of context/lifecycle plumbing, dependency direction, physical crate
    62	placement, and full-coverage batched/resumable load outcomes so a future I/O-free lifecycle can consume
    63	the same kernel a blocking lifecycle consumes today.

     1	# BS1 — Svelte compiler-output conformance train
     2	
     3	**Status:** PROPOSED / LOCKED. **Class:** Framework subsystem.
     4	**Predecessor:** B4.
     5	
     6	## Objective
     7	
     8	Deliver Svelte compiler correctness on the final B2–B4 substrate for exact
     9	`svelte@5.56.8`.
    10	
    11	## Owned scope
    12	
    13	- Svelte-owned semantic model and product plans;
    14	- client and server JavaScript; development and production;
    15	- runes and legacy behavior only where the capability lock claims them;
    16	- Svelte-native helpers, effects, blocks, events, bindings, actions, transitions,
    17	  animations, components, dynamic elements/components, DOM, and server topology;
    18	- stores, context, slots/children, snippets, boundaries, async behavior, namespaces,
    19	  hydration-compatible output, custom elements, whitespace/comments;
    20	- diagnostics, maps, PublicApi/TSC/declaration/tooling products; and
    21	- the complete accepted official-core Svelte pack.
    22	
    23	BS1 does not implement a Svelte runtime, use an official compiler in production, or
    24	automatically widen Verter's product API because the official compiler returns an
    25	extra artifact.
    26	
    27	## Required exits
    28	
    29	`FC-SVELTE-001`, `FC-HYDRATION-001`, `FC-TS-001`, `FC-ATOMIC-001`,
    30	`FC-ZERO-WORK-001`, and applicable `FC-PERF-001` cells pass. Every supported cell has
    31	no blocked official case or semantic known-divergence. Structural and dependency
    32	proofs demonstrate that no Vue semantic, IR, lowering, helper, hydration, event,
    33	component, or SSR assumption remains anywhere in Svelte implementation paths. Every
    34	corresponding BF3 guard is removed.
    35	
    36	## Abort/rescope
    37	
    38	Stop for an unlocked compatibility change, an unsupported official mode presented as
    39	success, an output requiring runtime patching, or any design that bases Svelte on Vue.
     1	# CM1 — Component-meta request-view materialization and runtime-prop type regression correction
     2	
     3	**Status:** DRAFT — authored for maintainer review; no AMD ratifies it yet. **Class:** subsystem
     4	(`program-dag.toml`). **Predecessors:** `BV1`, `BS1` (both `ACCEPTED`/`IN_PROGRESS` per the ledger at
     5	authoring time — see `docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml`).
     6	
     7	## Context
     8	
     9	A beta.4 regression intake (maintainer-ratified) ran `pikax/vue-benchmarks` against Verter versus
    10	published `@verter/*@0.0.1-beta.3` and found two component-meta regressions: exposed bindings
    11	(`defineExpose`) silently losing their type, and runtime prop constructors (`defineProps({ label:
    12	String })`) silently losing their type. A bounded, read-only investigation reproduced both in-repo
    13	(`crates/verter_session/tests/cases/findbc_regression.rs`, 12 tests, 9 red) and a ratified architecture
    14	ruling (Codex xhigh, 2026-08-20) turned the investigation into repair, path, and placement decisions.
    15	This charter turns that ruling into an executable charter. It does not reopen the ruling's REPAIR,
    16	PATH, or PLACEMENT decisions — see "Rulings applied" below.
    17	
    18	## There are two distinct defects, not one — this is the central finding
    19	
    20	The maintainer's original directive hypothesised a single defect: a `defineExpose`d/`defineProps`d
    21	position reaching `ComponentMetaOutputError::UnraisableSource` — *"the source has no live graph
    22	representation under the request view"* (`meta_resolve/output.rs:562-564`, the `exposed[].type` lane at
    23	`:376`). The in-repo investigation instead reproduced a **silent** degrade: the exposed/prop position
    24	never reaches a `Present` source at all — it resolves `SourcePosition::Absent`, which is a documented,
    25	intentional **success** path (`meta_resolve/projectors/output_sink/envelope.rs:154`) rendering
    26	`TypeExpr::Unknown(UnknownValue::missing_output())` with no error.
    27	
    28	The ruling holds these are **mutually exclusive control-flow states, not one defect presenting two
    29	ways**: `Absent` returns success; `UnraisableSource` can only arise once a `Present(source)` enters the
    30	strict raise (`raise_semantic_type_source_to_hot_strict`,
    31	`project_semantic_dispatch/semantic_source.rs:428`) and that raise yields no graph handle
    32	(`output_sink.rs:1221`, `:1273`) against a disposition the sink does not accept as a legitimate carrier.
    33	Both the NAPI scalar and batch routes preserve this failure identically (`crates/verter_napi/src/meta.rs:280,303`;
    34	`component_meta_host.rs:73`). **Both remain independent beta.4 blockers.** CM1 is not complete until
    35	both are closed, each proven by its own reproducing, discriminating test:
    36	
    37	- **Finding B/C (reproduced): `Absent → Unknown`.** The exposed/prop binding never gets offered a
    38	  source at all. Root-caused below.
    39	- **The benchmark's `Present → UnraisableSource`.** A binding DOES reach a `Present` source, but the
    40	  strict raise cannot produce a graph handle for it. Not yet root-caused in-repo — the investigation did
    41	  not have a fixture that reaches this state. **CM1 owns constructing or isolating a minimized fixture
    42	  that genuinely reaches `Present` and fails the raise, tracing it to its owning producer, and correcting
    43	  it there.**
    44	
    45	Closing only the `Absent→Unknown` path and treating the hard error as the same bug leaves a release
    46	blocker armed and shipping. Do not demote the hard-error case to `Absent` or `Unknown` to make it
    47	disappear — the strict output error is PREFERABLE to an invented type.
    48	
    49	## Established root cause
    50	
    51	### Finding B — `defineExpose` entries never offered to macro-type expansion
    52	
    53	`resolve_exposed_type` (`verter_semantic/src/analysis/component_meta.rs`) only sees a name if the
    54	general macro-argument-type expansion's binding-entry admission gate,
    55	`component_meta_binding_type_entries` (`verter_session/src/host_manage/eval_env.rs:907-956`, gate at
    56	`:938`), offers it. That gate admits only when `PreparedValueDecl.type_annotation.classification` is
    57	non-`Absent` — but `PreparedValueDecl` separately carries signatures
    58	(`verter_semantic/src/analysis/type_solver/prepared.rs:390`) and object-shape facts (`:395`) that a
    59	plain `function` declaration or a call-initialized `const` (`ref(0)`, `computed(...)`) uses instead
    60	(function declarations intentionally lower with no value annotation plus a signature,
    61	`type_eval_build.rs:2823`). The gate has no branch for either, so both are silently dropped before any
    62	raise/dispatch step runs — confirmed in-repo for methods, refs/computed, and full-API fixtures, typed
    63	and untyped alike.
    64	
    65	A further unresolved residual: an *explicitly annotated* call-initializer (`const count: Ref<number> =
    66	ref(0)`) should already classify `Direct` (explicit annotations become `Direct` at
    67	`fact_projection.rs:140`; an untyped call's expression source becomes `Direct` at `:101`) but still
    68	fails in the investigation's isolation test. The owner/lookup/preparation handoff has an unresolved
    69	divergence somewhere between those facts and the admission gate's read of them.
    70	
    71	Separately, `resolve_exposed_type` (`component_meta.rs:2801`) collapses `ResolvedTypeOutcome::Failed`
    72	and `::Absent` to the same `None` — a binding that *was* offered but failed to prepare is
    73	indistinguishable from one that was never offered, so a genuine preparation failure also renders as
    74	silent `Unknown` instead of failing strictly.
    75	
    76	### Finding C — runtime prop constructors are display-only on the macro path

The current validator is insufficient: at `3cb224033` it returns `OK` for all 64 blocks even though BS1 is `IN_PROGRESS` with no bound charter and authority existing only in an external prose ruling ([program-state.toml:628](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/program-state.toml:628)). That passes because evidence/charter binding starts only at `REVIEW` ([validate-program-state.mjs:815](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/validate-program-state.mjs:815)) and an empty `enabling_amendment` bypasses the authority check entirely ([validate-program-state.mjs:1018](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/validate-program-state.mjs:1018)).

No block may advance beyond BS1 until the following is implemented.

### 1. Authority model

Adopt repository-local, machine-readable block authorization records:

```text
docs/arch/refactor/rev11/authority/
  documents/*.toml
  ratifications/*.toml
  blocks/<block-id>.toml
  manifest.json                 # deterministic generated index
```

Each document record names a stable ID, kind (`CHARTER`, `AMENDMENT`, `RULING`, `ADR`, `CONTRACT`), repository-relative path, SHA-256, applicable blocks, prerequisite document IDs, typed effects, and effect-level supersessions.

Each ratification is an immutable decision event: `RATIFY`, `REVOKE`, or `SUPERSEDE`; subject ID; previous decision ID; maintainer identity; decision memo path and digest. Status is derived from the acyclic decision graph—never from dates or “last file wins.”

Each block authorization contains exactly one charter ID and the complete authority closure. The ledger gains:

```toml
authorization_id = "AUTH-BS1-..."
authorization_digest = "<sha256>"
```

`authorization_digest` is a domain-separated SHA-256 over the block record, its ratification records, all referenced authority records, and the raw bytes of every referenced document.

For every execution-bearing status—`READY`, `IN_PROGRESS`, `REVIEW`, `PRIVATE_CHECKPOINT`, `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED`, `ACCEPTED`—the validator must prove:

- the authorization exists, belongs to that block, and is currently ratified;
- its one charter exists and its digest matches both disk and `charter_digest`;
- every transitive `requires` authority is included;
- every active ruling whose `applies_to_blocks` includes the block is included, preventing selective omission;
- no cited document/effect is revoked or superseded;
- the computed authorization digest equals the ledger;
- the effective-state reducer reports no contradiction.

`BLOCKED`, `RESCOPE_REQUIRED`, `ABORTED`, and `SUPERSEDED` may exist without execution authority because they do not certify that work legally began.

Reject the alternatives:

- A document-local status field cannot express the complete block authority chain or partial supersession.
- A “signed” ledger row is invalid: the orchestrator is the ledger writer ([governance.md:181](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/governance.md:181)), and the repository has no signature-verification infrastructure. `ratified_by` is attribution, not cryptographic proof.
- Digest-binding documents is mandatory but insufficient without ratification, applicability, closure, and supersession.
- Markdown `**Status:**` lines must be replaced as enforcement. They may remain only as generator-owned display text. The validator must stop parsing English with `/ratified/`; that is the current fragile mechanism ([validate-program-state.mjs:985](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/validate-program-state.mjs:985)).

The irreducibly human step is confirming that a maintainer actually issued the decision and that its typed effects completely capture the prose. Everything after that—identity, closure, status, applicability, and transition legality—is automated.

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none; program outcome—none.

### 2. Ruling custody and binding

Create `docs/arch/refactor/rev11/rulings/`. Store one curated decision document per ruling, containing only facts relied upon, decision, typed-effect explanation, supersessions, and explicit ADR/DAG/outcome impact. Raw session transcripts may be preserved under `evidence/rulings/`, but they are not authority.

Every ruling receives a stable ID and an authority document record. Blocks cite rulings through their block-authorization record, not prose filenames. External paths, conversation history, and scratchpads categorically have no binding force, consistent with the existing rule that prior conversation is not repository state ([agent-orchestration.md:49](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/agent-orchestration.md:49)).

Supersession must operate on effect IDs, not merely whole documents. The flow reconciliation supersedes only parts of D1 Fork 2 while retaining other D1 decisions ([reconciliation:20247](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-C1-D1-FLOW-FILE-RECONCILIATION.md:20247)); document-level replacement would erase valid rulings.

Import and ratify, at minimum, the C1 four forks, C1 addendum, D1 six forks, C2 five forks, CM1 findings, flow reconciliation, and BS1 authority/completion decisions before another transition. The current C1 charter merely names an unavailable ruling ([C1.md:414](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/C1.md:414)).

Migration must expose—not silently repair—unapplied decisions. For example, the external C2 ruling requires `B6 -> C2` and a formal DAG amendment ([C2 ruling:16061](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-C2-FIVE-FORKS.md:16061)), while the current DAG still lists `B3`, `B5`, and `C1` ([program-dag.toml:177](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/program-dag.toml:177)). The hardened system must fail until separately ratified; this ruling does not grant that amendment.

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—no new edge authorized; program outcome—none.

### 3. Effective-state view

Implement `scripts/generate-program-effective-state.mjs` over a shared pure reducer used directly by both validators.

Inputs:

- exact DAG bytes;
- exact ledger bytes;
- authority records, ratifications, block authorizations, and referenced documents;
- any ledger-bound stack windows and checkpoint records;
- all input SHA-256s.

Output: deterministic, sorted `docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/effective-program-state.json`, containing input digests and, per block, class, predecessors, status, authorization closure, active/superseded effects, effective owners/dispositions/obligations, checkpoint state, and next legal transitions.

The committed JSON is for review only. Validators recompute the model in memory; `--check` requires the committed view to match byte-for-byte. A stale generated view is never trusted as input.

The reducer must fail—never choose “last wins”—on this contradiction taxonomy:

- `SINGLETON_CONFLICT`: two active values for one subject/facet/milestone.
- `POLARITY_CONFLICT`: require/forbid, add/remove, move/retain/delete, supported/refused.
- `HANDOFF_CONFLICT`: predecessor postcondition contradicts successor precondition. This catches C1 moving `flow_slice_content.rs` while D1 expected it not to move ([D1 ruling:12355](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-D1-SIX-FORKS.md:12355)).
- `CARDINALITY_CONFLICT`: multiple sole owners, writers, acceptance blocks, production routes, or oracle sources.
- `DAG_EFFECT_CONFLICT`: required/forbidden edge or block disagrees with the DAG; state/DAG/authorization block sets differ.
- `SUPERSESSION_CONFLICT`: missing targets, cycles, multiple active leaves, or citation of a superseded effect.
- `SCOPE_OVERLAP_CONFLICT`: concurrent blocks claim the same exclusive artifact, writer, generated store, or cutover.
- `OBLIGATION_CONFLICT`: an acceptance/capability/debt/gate row is simultaneously required and `N/A`, transferred without a successor, or declared proven and unproven.
- `ORACLE_CONFLICT`: an axis is both mandatory and omitted; official-oracle and candidate-output sources compete; required feature selection is absent.
- `REFERENCE_CONFLICT`: unknown or duplicated IDs, ambiguous paths, missing effects, or an authorization referencing another block’s charter.

Mechanics cannot detect omitted facts, semantic contradictions hidden in prose, two differently named subjects that are aliases, dishonest/incomplete effect encoding, whether a test truly proves its claim, or whether the named human actually approved a record. Those remain mandatory human review responsibilities.

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none; program outcome—none.

### 4. Mutation testing

Refactor both validators into one registry of independently falsifiable check variants. Current validators append anonymous strings directly ([validate-program-state.mjs:387](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/validate-program-state.mjs:387), [stack-window-lib.mjs:72](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:72)); that makes completeness unprovable.

Each `defineCheck` entry must contain:

- stable `check_id` and `variant_id`;
- fixture profile;
- evaluator;
- one or more mutation factories;
- applicable entry points;
- source citation.

Diagnostics become `VIOLATION[check_id/variant_id]`. The mutation runner automatically enumerates the registry and, for every mutation:

1. proves the valid seed passes;
2. proves serialized input changed;
3. proves the target check was evaluated on non-zero subjects;
4. proves the mutant fails;
5. proves the emitted diagnostic contains that exact check/variant ID.

Extra violations may occur, but the owning check must fire. Parameterized fields generate one mutant per declared field automatically.

`defineCheck` rejects an empty mutation set, and the registry meta-test asserts `registered variants == executed mutation variants`. Thus adding a check or branch without a mutation fails without maintaining a second list. Shared stack-window checks retain one implementation and declare coverage through both entry points, preserving the current single-model intent ([stack-window-lib.mjs:355](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:355)).

Add registered oracle mutations:

- Stale record: alter generator input or a committed record in a copied golden store and require official `--check` to fail. Preserve the stronger existing pattern that coherently updates the manifest so content addressing alone cannot catch it ([golden-provenance.spec.mjs:158](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/packages/framework-conformance-harness/test/golden-provenance.spec.mjs:158)).
- Missing/corrupt cache: use isolated cache paths; assert setup fails before Cargo/comparison, emits zero comparison events, and names provisioning. A valid-cache control must assert all expected tests are selected and execute. The existing distinction between missing and unusable cache is the correct basis ([gate-selftest.mjs:7247](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/gate-selftest.mjs:7247)).
- Candidate-poisoned golden: replace a copied golden payload with divergent candidate output, update its manifest coherently, then regenerate/check solely through the pinned official oracle; it must fail. Bind the sanctioned generator’s transitive implementation digest and oracle closure in authority, so changing generator plus goldens also invalidates authorization. Comparator code remains read-only—the existing operational test already proves comparisons do not mutate golden bytes ([golden-immutability.spec.mjs:47](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/packages/framework-conformance-harness/test/golden-immutability.spec.mjs:47)).

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none; program outcome—none.

### 5. Internal checkpoints with atomic acceptance

Use the existing `ATOMIC_REVIEW` model: private layers may repeat the final block’s ID, exactly one final layer is mergeable, and the combined tip receives final review ([stacked-prs.md:43](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:43)). Do not create synthetic DAG blocks.

Add digest-bound records at `ledger/checkpoints/<block>/<sequence>.toml`. Each records:

- block/checkpoint/preceding-checkpoint IDs;
- authority and effective-state digests;
- exact base/candidate SHA/tree and stack snapshot;
- cumulative patch/generated/evidence digests;
- closed charter-exit IDs covered;
- per-exit `PROVEN`, `UNPROVEN`, `BLOCKING`, or authority-backed `NOT_APPLICABLE`;
- commands, selected/executed counts, raw-log digests;
- findings, dispositions, reviewer identity, checkpoint verdict;
- invalidation or carry-forward/equivalence record.

A passing checkpoint gates only the next internal phase/layer. It never creates a program-state row, accepted SHA, maintainer decision, predecessor satisfaction, or final review verdict. Every private layer remains non-mergeable and carries the acceptance block’s ID, which the current validator already recognizes structurally ([stack-window-lib.mjs:253](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:253)).

Any candidate change invalidates affected checkpoint approval; evidence may carry only through an explicit equivalence record and reattestation. Final `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED` still requires every exit proven and all required mandates bound to the complete final candidate, matching exact-SHA governance ([governance.md:249](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/governance.md:249)).

For BS1, the complete exit matrix must exist before the first checkpoint, derived from its required exits ([BS1.md:27](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/BS1.md:27)). The seven-fix checkpoint, oracle/gate checkpoint, capability/performance checkpoint, and final combined checkpoint would have surfaced the stale verdicts and unproven rows before escalation. No row may become `N/A` without a ratified rescope—the correction expressly held hydration/performance as blocked rather than absent ([completion correction:13](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/MAINTAINER-RULING-BS1-COMPLETION-CORRECTION.md:13)).

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none for internal checkpoints; program outcome—none. A truly independently acceptable split would require a separate future DAG amendment and is not authorized here.

RULING 1 — Replace prose/document status gates with digest-bound, ratified block-authorization records in a repository authority registry.  
RULING 2 — Move every binding ruling into `rev11/rulings/`, bind it through typed effect records, and treat all external rulings as nonbinding.  
RULING 3 — Generate one fail-closed effective-state model with explicit effect-level supersession and the contradiction taxonomy above.  
RULING 4 — Make every validator/oracle check a registered variant with a co-located, automatically executed mutation; uncovered checks fail the suite.  
RULING 5 — Represent large-block checkpoints as digest-bound same-block private layers that gate internal progress but can never satisfy program acceptance.  
SEQUENCING — Land the mutation registry first, because authorization and effective-state enforcement must demonstrate discrimination as they are introduced; then authority/ruling migration, effective-state generation, and finally checkpoint enforcement.

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—no new edge authorized; program outcome—none.

### 3. Effective-state view

Implement `scripts/generate-program-effective-state.mjs` over a shared pure reducer used directly by both validators.

Inputs:

- exact DAG bytes;
- exact ledger bytes;
- authority records, ratifications, block authorizations, and referenced documents;
- any ledger-bound stack windows and checkpoint records;
- all input SHA-256s.

Output: deterministic, sorted `docs/arch/architecture-lock/ledger/effective-program-state.json`, containing input digests and, per block, class, predecessors, status, authorization closure, active/superseded effects, effective owners/dispositions/obligations, checkpoint state, and next legal transitions.

The committed JSON is for review only. Validators recompute the model in memory; `--check` requires the committed view to match byte-for-byte. A stale generated view is never trusted as input.

The reducer must fail—never choose “last wins”—on this contradiction taxonomy:

- `SINGLETON_CONFLICT`: two active values for one subject/facet/milestone.
- `POLARITY_CONFLICT`: require/forbid, add/remove, move/retain/delete, supported/refused.
- `HANDOFF_CONFLICT`: predecessor postcondition contradicts successor precondition. This catches C1 moving `flow_slice_content.rs` while D1 expected it not to move ([D1 ruling:12355](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/ARCH-RULING-D1-SIX-FORKS.md:12355)).
- `CARDINALITY_CONFLICT`: multiple sole owners, writers, acceptance blocks, production routes, or oracle sources.
- `DAG_EFFECT_CONFLICT`: required/forbidden edge or block disagrees with the DAG; state/DAG/authorization block sets differ.
- `SUPERSESSION_CONFLICT`: missing targets, cycles, multiple active leaves, or citation of a superseded effect.
- `SCOPE_OVERLAP_CONFLICT`: concurrent blocks claim the same exclusive artifact, writer, generated store, or cutover.
- `OBLIGATION_CONFLICT`: an acceptance/capability/debt/gate row is simultaneously required and `N/A`, transferred without a successor, or declared proven and unproven.
- `ORACLE_CONFLICT`: an axis is both mandatory and omitted; official-oracle and candidate-output sources compete; required feature selection is absent.
- `REFERENCE_CONFLICT`: unknown or duplicated IDs, ambiguous paths, missing effects, or an authorization referencing another block’s charter.

Mechanics cannot detect omitted facts, semantic contradictions hidden in prose, two differently named subjects that are aliases, dishonest/incomplete effect encoding, whether a test truly proves its claim, or whether the named human actually approved a record. Those remain mandatory human review responsibilities.

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none; program outcome—none.

### 4. Mutation testing

Refactor both validators into one registry of independently falsifiable check variants. Current validators append anonymous strings directly ([validate-program-state.mjs:387](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/validate-program-state.mjs:387), [stack-window-lib.mjs:72](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:72)); that makes completeness unprovable.

Each `defineCheck` entry must contain:

- stable `check_id` and `variant_id`;
- fixture profile;
- evaluator;
- one or more mutation factories;
- applicable entry points;
- source citation.

Diagnostics become `VIOLATION[check_id/variant_id]`. The mutation runner automatically enumerates the registry and, for every mutation:

1. proves the valid seed passes;
2. proves serialized input changed;
3. proves the target check was evaluated on non-zero subjects;
4. proves the mutant fails;
5. proves the emitted diagnostic contains that exact check/variant ID.

Extra violations may occur, but the owning check must fire. Parameterized fields generate one mutant per declared field automatically.

`defineCheck` rejects an empty mutation set, and the registry meta-test asserts `registered variants == executed mutation variants`. Thus adding a check or branch without a mutation fails without maintaining a second list. Shared stack-window checks retain one implementation and declare coverage through both entry points, preserving the current single-model intent ([stack-window-lib.mjs:355](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:355)).

Add registered oracle mutations:

- Stale record: alter generator input or a committed record in a copied golden store and require official `--check` to fail. Preserve the stronger existing pattern that coherently updates the manifest so content addressing alone cannot catch it ([golden-provenance.spec.mjs:158](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/packages/framework-conformance-harness/test/golden-provenance.spec.mjs:158)).
- Missing/corrupt cache: use isolated cache paths; assert setup fails before Cargo/comparison, emits zero comparison events, and names provisioning. A valid-cache control must assert all expected tests are selected and execute. The existing distinction between missing and unusable cache is the correct basis ([gate-selftest.mjs:7247](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/gate-selftest.mjs:7247)).
- Candidate-poisoned golden: replace a copied golden payload with divergent candidate output, update its manifest coherently, then regenerate/check solely through the pinned official oracle; it must fail. Bind the sanctioned generator’s transitive implementation digest and oracle closure in authority, so changing generator plus goldens also invalidates authorization. Comparator code remains read-only—the existing operational test already proves comparisons do not mutate golden bytes ([golden-immutability.spec.mjs:47](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/packages/framework-conformance-harness/test/golden-immutability.spec.mjs:47)).

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none; program outcome—none.

### 5. Internal checkpoints with atomic acceptance

Use the existing `ATOMIC_REVIEW` model: private layers may repeat the final block’s ID, exactly one final layer is mergeable, and the combined tip receives final review ([stacked-prs.md:43](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/contracts/stacked-prs.md:43)). Do not create synthetic DAG blocks.

Add digest-bound records at `ledger/checkpoints/<block>/<sequence>.toml`. Each records:

- block/checkpoint/preceding-checkpoint IDs;
- authority and effective-state digests;
- exact base/candidate SHA/tree and stack snapshot;
- cumulative patch/generated/evidence digests;
- closed charter-exit IDs covered;
- per-exit `PROVEN`, `UNPROVEN`, `BLOCKING`, or authority-backed `NOT_APPLICABLE`;
- commands, selected/executed counts, raw-log digests;
- findings, dispositions, reviewer identity, checkpoint verdict;
- invalidation or carry-forward/equivalence record.

A passing checkpoint gates only the next internal phase/layer. It never creates a program-state row, accepted SHA, maintainer decision, predecessor satisfaction, or final review verdict. Every private layer remains non-mergeable and carries the acceptance block’s ID, which the current validator already recognizes structurally ([stack-window-lib.mjs:253](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/scripts/lib/stack-window-lib.mjs:253)).

Any candidate change invalidates affected checkpoint approval; evidence may carry only through an explicit equivalence record and reattestation. Final `ACCEPTANCE_RECOMMENDED` still requires every exit proven and all required mandates bound to the complete final candidate, matching exact-SHA governance ([governance.md:249](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/governance.md:249)).

For BS1, the complete exit matrix must exist before the first checkpoint, derived from its required exits ([BS1.md:27](<MACHINE_ROOT>/verter/docs/arch/refactor/rev11/charters/BS1.md:27)). The seven-fix checkpoint, oracle/gate checkpoint, capability/performance checkpoint, and final combined checkpoint would have surfaced the stale verdicts and unproven rows before escalation. No row may become `N/A` without a ratified rescope—the correction expressly held hydration/performance as blocked rather than absent ([completion correction:13](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-carlosrodrigues-Documents-dev-verter/cad766b2-94b4-4208-a25d-0fed78cc40e6/scratchpad/rulings/MAINTAINER-RULING-BS1-COMPLETION-CORRECTION.md:13)).

Impact: accepted ADR—none; DAG—none for internal checkpoints; program outcome—none. A truly independently acceptable split would require a separate future DAG amendment and is not authorized here.

RULING 1 — Replace prose/document status gates with digest-bound, ratified block-authorization records in a repository authority registry.  
RULING 2 — Move every binding ruling into `rev11/rulings/`, bind it through typed effect records, and treat all external rulings as nonbinding.  
RULING 3 — Generate one fail-closed effective-state model with explicit effect-level supersession and the contradiction taxonomy above.  
RULING 4 — Make every validator/oracle check a registered variant with a co-located, automatically executed mutation; uncovered checks fail the suite.  
RULING 5 — Represent large-block checkpoints as digest-bound same-block private layers that gate internal progress but can never satisfy program acceptance.  
SEQUENCING — Land the mutation registry first, because authorization and effective-state enforcement must demonstrate discrimination as they are introduced; then authority/ruling migration, effective-state generation, and finally checkpoint enforcement.
